docs.t: Judge Beth Labson Freeman (N.D. Cal.) — Briefing and formatting (trap)
docs.x: Judge Beth Labson Freeman, N.D. Cal.. Briefing and formatting (trap): Any stipulated briefing schedule must leave at least 14 days (preferably 21) between the final brief and the hearing. All text, including footnotes and quotations, must be at least 12-point and double-spaced. No citations to authority or evidence in footnotes; generally no more than 5 footnotes per brief, and excessive ones are disregarded. No incorporation by reference of arguments from other briefs (except among parties sharing page limits). Highlight cited portions of depositions and long documents in yellow only. Evidentiary objections go in the brief. Argument supporting a request for judicial notice counts against the page limit. Proposed orders go in Word to BLFpo@cand.uscourts.gov the day they are e-filed. Do not communicate ex parte with the judge or chambers.

docs.x: Judge Beth Labson Freeman, N.D. Cal.. Summary judgment and Daubert timing: Summary judgment motions must be heard at least 90 days before trial; the court generally reserves a compliant date at the initial CMC. Daubert motions must be heard at least 60 days before trial, or may instead be brought as motions in limine (one expert per motion).

docs.x: Judge Beth Labson Freeman, N.D. Cal.. If the court allows narrower sealing than the public versions reflect, the filing party must refile public versions within 7 days unless a renewed motion or declaration is filed.

docs.x: Judge Beth Labson Freeman, N.D. Cal.. docs.t: Judge Beth Labson Freeman (N.D. Cal.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Beth Labson Freeman, N.D. Cal.. Trial: Trial runs Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Tuesday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Thursdays are typically dark. docs.x: Judge William Orrick III, N.D. Cal.. Discovery and filings: Lead trial counsel must meet and confer in person or by video (letters, emails, calls don’t count); then one joint statement of five pages covering all disputes, certifying compliance (or two-page individual statements explaining why no joint one). No exhibits except the requests and responses. Protective or ESI orders: use the model or justify departures by declaration with a redline. No courtesy copies, except manually filed media and binders of exhibits over 100 pages for TRO, PI, and summary judgment motions. One summary judgment motion per party. Serve all the judge’s standing orders on every party and file a certificate of service.

docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Hearings and calendar: Civil motions Thursdays at 9 a.m., by reservation only through the courtroom deputy (ejdcrd@cand.uscourts.gov). File and notice the motion within 14 days of reserving or the date is vacated without notice. docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Requests to appear remotely are decided hearing by hearing and require an administrative request and proposed order filed at least 1 week before the hearing. The moving party on a motion will not be allowed to appear remotely. Absent extraordinary circumstances, no remote appearance for parties or counsel who live or have an office within the district’s counties (the 2026 Scheduling Notes list all 15; the 2022 standing order lists the Bay Area and San Jose Division counties).

docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Motions and filings
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Motions and filings: Follow the Local Rule page limits unless leave is obtained in advance; footnotes at least 12-point and double-spaced. Absent good cause, allow at least 14 days between the final brief and the hearing. Proposed orders are not needed for most substantive motions; submit them only for administrative motions, ex parte applications, and motions seeking specific injunctive relief or factual findings (e.g., class settlement approval, attorneys’ fees), emailed in Word to ejdpo@cand.uscourts.gov. Exchange and email demonstratives to the deputy at least 48 hours before a hearing. Amended complaints must attach a redline. The judge does not read or respond to letters or letter briefs, even if docketed; request action by stipulation and proposed order or motion. No ex parte contact with chambers.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Summary judgment (trap): One motion per party unless permitted; noncompliant motions may be summarily terminated. Evidentiary objections go in the brief, not a separate filing. Daubert motions may be heard no later than the dispositive motion hearing date. The movant files a separate statement chart (no more than 15 pages) listing elements, material facts, and evidence, and serves it in word-processing format; the response adds no more than 5 pages. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted, and each statement needs the prescribed attestation. Cross-motions: meet and confer before the deadline; only four briefs are allowed (opposition/cross-motion 25 pages, reply/opposition 15, final reply 15, filed within 7 days), and the fourth brief must be filed at least 14 days before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Sealing (trap): Strict compliance with Civil L.R. 79-5 is required, and nonconforming motions may be summarily terminated. File a separate sealing motion for each pleading; no omnibus motions. When the document to be sealed is a motion, also file the redacted motion as its own docket entry (using the “motion” event and the reserved hearing date) at the same time as the sealing motion.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Case management and junior lawyers
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Any firm with more than 30 lawyers nationwide must include in the joint CMC statement a specific plan, naming individual lawyers, for giving junior lawyers (6 or fewer years out) chances to argue motions, take depositions, and examine witnesses. Motion papers may request a hearing for a junior lawyer to argue.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Trial, settlement, and continuances
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Trial, settlement, and continuances: Trial days are Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday; the posted hours differ (the standing order says 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., the calendar summary 9 to noon and 1:30 to 4:30, and the 2026 Scheduling Notes 9 to 5). Continuances are disfavored, and jury costs may be assessed for late settlement notice or failure to proceed to trial.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Criminal matters
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Criminal matters: Email the deputy a draft (unsigned) plea agreement at least 3 court days before the hearing. The judge does not use the court’s guilty plea application form for open pleas and conducts the plea colloquy in the normal course. Stipulations and proposed orders to continue a hearing are due 3 court days before it.

docs.t: Judge Edward Davila (N.D. Cal.) — Patent cases
docs.x: Judge Edward Davila, N.D. Cal.. Patent cases: Disclosure disputes and contention amendments go to the magistrate judge. Only terms designated “most significant” are construed; more than 10 requires a Civil L.R. 7-11(b) administrative motion by the joint statement deadline showing good cause. Briefs are 25/25/15 pages. Default tutorial and hearing is a half day: 30 minutes per side for the tutorial and one hour per side for argument, term by term. Live testimony needs a motion at least 14 days before; exchange exhibits and lodge three bound copies 1 week before. Summary judgment on infringement or invalidity requires one joint statement of undisputed facts (no separate statements) and, after briefing closes, a binder for the court with joint summary charts in the Attachment B format. The post-construction CMC statement is due 7 days before the conference.

docs.x: Judge John J. Tuchi, D. Ariz.. Summary judgment, Daubert, and motions (trap): Daubert motions are due with dispositive motions, by the dispositive motion deadline. One summary judgment motion per party (or parties sharing a lawyer) without leave. Statements of facts and controverting statements are limited to 10 pages and should include only the facts relied on. Noncompliance with LRCiv 7.2, failure to file a response, or failure to appear for argument may be deemed consent to the motion under LRCiv 7.2(i). If no dispositive motion is pending when the deadline passes, plaintiff must file a Notice of Readiness for a status conference within 10 days.

docs.t: Judge John J. Tuchi (D. Ariz.) — Experts
docs.x: Judge John J. Tuchi, D. Ariz.. Experts: Expert disclosures must be full and complete under Rule 26(a)(2)(A)–(C), with full Rule 26(a)(2)(B) reports for retained experts and for employees who regularly give expert testimony. Reports must set out the expected direct testimony and the reasons for it; absent truly extraordinary circumstances, no supplementation after the set dates. No expert depositions before the expert disclosures are made. Interrogatories are limited to 25, including discrete subparts; depositions follow Rules 30 and 31.

docs.x: Judge John J. Tuchi, D. Ariz.. Patent, ERISA, IDEA, and administrative-record cases: Patent cases require infringement and invalidity contentions before the Markman hearing (citing the N.D. Cal. Patent Local Rules as a guide), a claim construction briefing schedule ending in a joint chart, and affirmative expert disclosures 30 days after the claim construction order (rebuttal 30 days later). Cases reviewed on an administrative record (ERISA or IDEA) get a separate scheduling order with deadlines for producing the administrative record, any conflict-of-interest discovery, disclosing materials a party says belong in the record, and filing the record. Plaintiff’s opening brief and defendant’s response are limited to 25 pages and the reply to 11 pages, each including any statement of facts.

Designation challenges go first through 14 days of written objection and negotiation.

docs.t: Judge John J. Tuchi (D. Ariz.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge John J. Tuchi, D. Ariz.. Trial conduct: Stand at the podium to address the court, jury, or witnesses; ask permission to approach a witness or the bench. One attorney per witness, and the one objecting on direct does the cross. Objections state only the ground or rule number, without argument before the jury. Use surnames, address remarks to the judge, and make no motions or stipulation requests in front of the jury. Offer only relevant deposition excerpts, highlighted yellow (plaintiff) or blue (defense). No food, gum, or drinks other than water; civility is mandatory. The civil and criminal juror questionnaires describe trial days of 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., Tuesday through Friday the first week, and Monday or Tuesday through Friday excluding Thursdays after that.

Give the deputy and judge a list of everyone at counsel table at the pretrial conference and, each trial day, that day’s witnesses and exhibits. Stand at the podium; do not approach the bench, witness, or clerk without permission, and hand papers to the deputy. One attorney per witness, and the attorney objecting on direct handles cross. Use surnames only, and don’t greet adverse witnesses. Object by saying “objection” and the basis or rule number only; no argument before the jury unless asked. No motions or stipulation offers in the jury’s presence.

docs.t: Judge G. Murray Snow (D. Ariz.) — Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge G. Murray Snow, D. Ariz.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Rule 16 conferences are telephonic; no headsets or speakerphones, and a poor connection means resetting the conference in person. In standard cases, exchange initial disclosures at least one week before the conference. In standard cases, meet under Rule 26(f) at least 21 days before the conference (10 calendar days in ERISA cases) and file the joint report at least 7 days before; plaintiff initiates. The standard report has 20 numbered paragraphs, including parent entities, a case statement of 3 pages or less, every party’s citizenship in diversity cases, any wish to file a dispositive motion before discovery, ESI, privilege, FRE 502(d), proportionality, and proposed dates falling on Fridays. Plan for trial within 18 months of the complaint. Trial counsel must attend with authority to stipulate; continuances only for good cause.

Co., 2009 WL 57053 (D. Ariz. Jan. 8, 2009): 20 interrogatories, 15 requests for production, and 20 requests for admission per side, subparts included, with deposition hours set in the order; no experts. The case is decided on opening, response, and reply merits briefs instead of Rule 56 motions, using Rule 56 page limits with no LRCiv 56.1 statement of facts, and the order sets a hearing on the briefs in Courtroom 602.

docs.t: Judge David G. Campbell (D. Ariz.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge David G. Campbell, D. Ariz.. Jury instructions: Civil: one joint list in three sections: Ninth Circuit models (full text, marked ST, PL, or DF and modified to fit the case), stipulated non-model instructions, and disputed non-model instructions numbered with authority, each followed by the objection, any alternative, and the objection to the alternative. Each instruction begins on a new page. Criminal: same approach in four sections (models, stipulated non-model, the government’s disputed, and the defendant’s disputed), with objections supported by authority.

docs.t: Judge David G. Campbell (D. Ariz.) — Criminal pretrial
docs.x: Judge David G. Campbell, D. Ariz.. Criminal pretrial: File 5 business days before the final pretrial conference a joint statement of the case, joint witness list, joint voir dire, joint jury instructions, joint verdict form, motions in limine, and other pretrial motions, and deliver a 3-hole-punched paper copy to the court. Responses are due 3 business days before; no replies. Trial counsel and the defendant must attend. Email voir dire, the statement of the case, and instructions in Word, and file a Notice to Court Reporter 5 business days before trial. Change of plea and admit/deny hearings, and evidentiary revocation hearings, are referred to a magistrate judge for findings and recommendations (order of July 17, 2014).

Mark exhibits before court, give the judge copies at the start of trial, and show exhibits to opposing counsel before offering them. Offer only relevant deposition portions: plaintiff highlights in yellow, defense in blue. No food, gum, or drinks other than water in cups. docs.x: Judge Steven Paul Logan, D. Ariz.. In civil cases, only a Stipulation and Order of Dismissal vacates trial; a notice of settlement or call does not, and day-of-trial dismissal may draw sanctions such as jury costs. In criminal cases, a stipulated motion to continue the final pretrial conference for a change of plea must be filed at least 7 days before it, and a plea less than 4 days before trial may lead to a show-cause hearing and sanctions.

docs.x: Judge John Z. Boyle, D. Ariz.. Discovery limits and timing: Depositions are limited to 7 hours each; Rules 30, 31, and 33 govern the number of depositions and interrogatories. Depositions must begin at least 5 business days before the discovery deadline (they may then run to the deadline), and written discovery must be served at least 45 days before it. Agreed extensions of response times do not move the deadlines. Objections must be specific; “general” or “global” objections are not considered.

docs.x: Judge John Z. Boyle, D. Ariz.. Experts: Rebuttal experts may respond only to opinions of initial experts, and each party gets one retained or specially employed expert per issue. Rule 26(a)(2)(A) disclosures must name treating physicians and other non-report experts, with Rule 26(a)(2)(C) summaries of facts and opinions detailed enough to give fair notice; a treating physician needs a full report for opinions formed outside the course of treatment. An untimely disclosed expert is excluded unless the need could not reasonably have been anticipated, the court and opponents were promptly notified, and the expert was promptly offered for deposition (Wong v. Regents).

Depositions must begin at least 5 business days before the discovery deadline (they may then run to the deadline), and written discovery must be served at least 45 days before it. Agreed extensions of response times do not move the deadlines. Objections must be specific; “general” or “global” objections are not considered.

An untimely disclosed expert is excluded unless the need could not reasonably have been anticipated, the court and opponents were promptly notified, and the expert was promptly offered for deposition (Wong v. Regents).

docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Social Security cases: deadlines (trap): The standing scheduling order controls over any prior order and over CM/ECF auto-deadlines. docs.x: Judge Jane Margaret Triche Milazzo, E.D. La.. docs.x: Judge Jane Margaret Triche Milazzo, E.D. La.. ERISA benefits cases (trap): Under the sample ERISA order, objections are due within 7 days. Within 90 days plaintiff must file a statement on completeness of the record. Discovery is limited per Fifth Circuit precedent (none on the factual basis of the medical claim); expanding it needs a prompt motion. The parties must contact the magistrate judge within 30 days to schedule a settlement conference held within 180 days; a briefing order follows.

docs.x: Judge Karen Wells Roby, E.D. La.. ESI conference and report (civil protocol): The judge’s civil ESI protocol is a framework the parties may adopt in full or adapt. docs.x: Judge Karen Wells Roby, E.D. La.. ESI search terms, privilege, and costs (trap): A producing party must disclose its search terms or methodology. Privileged or work-product material generated after the complaint need not be logged; the parties should confer on log scope, alternatives to document-by-document logs, and a Rule 502 non-waiver order. ESI is presumptively produced with searchable text in an agreed format (e.g., TIFF with text file). Each side generally bears its own costs, but the court may shift them on good cause. Not-reasonably-accessible objections must be stated with particularity, not boilerplate.

docs.t: Judge Michael B. North (E.D. La.) — Objections and privilege logs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael B. North, E.D. La.. Objections and privilege logs (trap): General and boilerplate objections (vague, overly broad, unduly burdensome, irrelevant, “unlikely to lead to the discovery of admissible evidence”) are prohibited. Support every objection or it will be overruled; burden objections need facts. If you answer “subject to” or “reserving” an objection, disclose whether you are actually withholding anything, or the objection will be found waived. You cannot object “to the extent” a request seeks privileged material without listing that material on a privilege log under Rule 26(b)(5).

docs.t: Judge Michael B. North (E.D. La.) — Discovery requests and depositions
docs.x: Judge Michael B. North, E.D. La.. No speaking objections (including “you can answer if you know”), interruptions, instructions not to answer except as Rule 30(c)(2) allows, or serial unfounded “form” objections. If an unresolvable dispute arises in a deposition, call chambers for direction.

docs.x: Judge Michael B. North, E.D. La.. Motion hearings and briefing: Motions are routinely set for hearing; expect a question-and-answer format rather than a repeat of the briefs. Deposition testimony is protected only if designated on the record and then identified in a Notice of Designation served within 14 days of transcript delivery. A nonmovant who fails to engage timely in the meet-and-confer can be sanctioned, including fees and costs of the motion or denial of later leave to amend. Parties should try not to oppose motions to amend filed before the initial Case Management Conference or within the Rule 26(f) Report or Rule 16 order deadlines.

docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. No separate briefing order generally issues, so waiting for one is no excus

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Follow Local Rule 56 except as modified. A response to a statement of facts must reprint each original fact statement, followed by the response, seriatim. The summary judgment deadline is set by order after the Post-Discovery Status/Settlement Conference. Expert depositions not relevant to Rule 56 motions are deferred until after the ruling.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and appearances
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Communications and appearances: No correspondence to the judge unless requested or approved. Do not contact law clerks; status and procedure questions go to the Deputy Clerk. Rescheduling requests may be phoned in only with all counsel on the line; otherwise file a motion. Phone participation is discouraged and considered case by case for good cause. No courtesy copies unless ordered or requested.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Confidential position letters (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Confidential position letters (trap): In jury cases only, each party must email a confidential position letter (facts, strengths and weaknesses, settlement posture) to bissoon_external@pawd.uscourts.gov at least 3 business days before the Initial Rule 16 Conference, the Post-Discovery Status Conference, and the Final Pretrial Conference. Do not file or share it; do not submit one in non-jury cases. In jury cases, counsel and clients (or persons with ultimate settlement authority, including insurers) must attend settlement conferences, including the Post-Discovery and Final Pretrial Conferences, in person; phone participation only with leave for good cause. Sanctions may follow if the person lacks ultimate authority.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Scheduling, ADR, and discovery
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Scheduling, ADR, and discovery: The Post-Discovery Status Conference is held no more than 30 days after discovery closes (also a settlement conference in jury cases). File the ADR stipulation (naming a proposed neutral) before the Initial Case Management Conference; discovery generally runs 150 days with mediation or early neutral evaluation, 120 with arbitration. For discovery disputes, confer, then call the court to set a conference instead of filing a motion; otherwise the motion will be denied without prejudice absent good cause. Deposition disputes may be phoned in jointly. Dispositive motions and ADR generally do not stay discovery. Extensions require a written motion with supporting facts and opposing counsel’s position.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Injunctions and TROs
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Injunctions and TROs: Avoid ex parte contact. No TRO issues if the opponent has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service cannot be accomplished, or if there is no affidavit or verified complaint under Rule 65(b)(1)(A).

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Trial: Trials run Monday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; no testimony on Fridays absent extraordinary circumstances. Optional trial briefs up to 15 pages, filed at least 1 week before trial. Exhibits are marked “P” and “D” (with an initial for multiple parties); demonstratives in openings need advance approval. One attorney per witness or point; no examination beyond recross. Submit a single agreed set of jury instructions and a verdict form using the Third Circuit Model Jury Instructions, with each side’s version and authority for disputed ones. Video testimony: notify the court in advance and do not file the recording. Bench trials: consecutively numbered proposed findings and conclusions, plus a supporting brief of up to 20 pages, are due within 20 days after the last trial day, with editable versions sent separately.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Proposed orders on extensions must include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language; more than five extensions will likely prompt a conference. Pre-plea PSRs require the defendant’s written consent in the form set out in the rules. Rule 11(c)(1)(C) pleas are generally deferred until after the PSR. Sentencing memoranda and supplemental information are due no later than 7 calendar days before sentencing; notify the court at least 2 weeks ahead if extensive testimony will be offered. Motions to travel must state the positions of the government and Probation/Pretrial Services.

docs.t: Judge Cathy Bissoon (W.D. Pa.) — Patent, bankruptcy, and Erie cases
docs.x: Judge Cathy Bissoon, W.D. Pa.. Patent, bankruptcy, and Erie cases: Patent cases follow the Local Patent Rules; the judge is a designated Patent Pilot Program judge. In bankruptcy appeals, the appellant’s brief is due 30 days after the notice of appeal. In Erie Division civil cases, Rule 16 conferences are by phone unless counsel is local to Pittsburgh; other conferences and trial take place in Erie.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Motions to dismiss: conferral certificate (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Motions to dismiss: conferral certificate (trap): Before any Rule 12(b) motion, the parties must meet and confer about whether the pleading defects can be cured by amendment, including with pro se parties. The motion must include a certificate of good-faith conferral, or it will be summarily denied. A nonmovant who fails to engage timely in the conferral may be sanctioned, including fees and costs of the motion and denial of later leave to amend.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Briefs and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Briefs and page limits (trap): Any motion seeking a substantive ruling needs a supporting brief filed with it; no briefs for extensions or continuances. Dispositive briefs are capped at 20 pages (excluding exhibits and fact statements) and all others at 10. Substantive arguments in footnotes are not considered or preserved. Replies are allowed without leave only for Rule 12(b), 12(c), and 56 motions, capped at 5 pages and due 7 days after service of the response. All other replies and any surreply need leave and are capped at 5 pages. Responses are due 21 days from service for dispositive motions (including motions to remand) and 7 days for non-dispositive motions, unless ordered otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Motion practice generally
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Motion practice generally: Communicate with the court by motion with a proposed order; the proposed order must state the specific relief, not just that the motion “is granted.” Conferences may be rescheduled by phone to the deputy clerk only with all counsel on the line. For routine motions (extensions, continuances, leave to amend), confer and state whether consent was obtained; omitting the other side’s position may lead to summary denial. Motions to amend must attach the draft amended pleading in redline or track changes, state all parties’ positions, and explain the new law or facts supporting amendment. Amendments as of right also need a redline copy attached. No courtesy copies of anything on CM/ECF unless requested. Oral argument only if the court decides; a party may request it.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motions until after a telephonic conference. After good-faith conferral, jointly call chambers or email deputy clerk Brian_Wright@pawd.uscourts.gov, copying the paralegal at Danielle_Crane@pawd.uscourts.gov. Notify the court at least 7 days before the relevant discovery cutoff if practicable; noncompliance means denial without prejudice. Disputes during depositions may be raised by a joint phone call. Discovery generally runs 150 days; extensions only for good cause and if counsel advanced the case. A dispositive motion or ADR does not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Confidential position letters (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Confidential position letters (trap): In jury cases only, each party emails a confidential position letter of 5 pages or less to wiegand_chambers@pawd.uscourts.gov at least 3 business days before every scheduled conference (initial case management, post-discovery, settlement, or pretrial). Do not file or share it. Cover the salient facts, candid strengths and weaknesses with likelihood of prevailing, estimated trial cost and time, relief sought, and settlement posture and history. No letters in non-jury cases.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and ADR
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and ADR: Initial case management conference ordinarily within 30 days after all answers or a Rule 12 ruling; lead trial counsel must participate. File the Rule 26(f) report and a fully completed ADR stipulation beforehand. ADR stipulations that are incomplete, lack a date certain, or set the session more than 60 days after the conference (without explaining why) will be stricken. Case management, post-discovery, and status conferences are generally telephonic; remote participation otherwise only for good cause. Settlement and final pretrial conferences are in person.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: A post-discovery status conference is held within 30 days after discovery closes; meet and confer beforehand on settlement and any planned summary judgment motion, and the court then sets deadlines. When responding to a statement of facts, reprint each original fact followed by the response, seriatim. Otherwise follow Local Rule 56.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement and pretrial
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Settlement and pretrial: Settlement conferences are for cases headed to jury trial. Lead trial counsel, client representatives, and any insurer representative (even with a coverage dispute) must attend in person with ultimate settlement authority, without needing to consult anyone. The same attendees must appear in person at the final pretrial conference. Motions in limine and Daubert deadlines are set by order. Confer first and file a Local Civil Rule 16.1.C.4 certificate. Each motion in limine (or each motion’s portion of an omnibus brief) is capped at 5 double-spaced pages.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: No TRO if the opposing party has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service cannot be made, or if it lacks a Rule 65(b)(1)(A) affidavit or verified complaint. Arrange any bond when filing. Support with affidavits attaching all relevant documents; responses should include affidavits. Be ready to argue and present witnesses immediately.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Objections, R&Rs, and bankruptcy appeals
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Objections, R&Rs, and bankruptcy appeals: Object on the record immediately; if no reporter is present, request one. Briefs on objections to a magistrate judge’s report and recommendation are capped at 15 pages. Bankruptcy appeals: appellant’s brief 30 days after the notice of appeal, appellee’s 30 days later, reply 14 days after that.

docs.t: Judge Christy C. Wiegand (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Christy C. Wiegand, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Confer before moving to extend the pretrial-motion deadline, and include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. File only after the status conference unless it falls after the deadline; premature motions are denied. Pre-plea presentence reports require the defendant’s written consent in the form set out in the procedures. Motions to travel must state the government’s and Pretrial Services’ positions. Protective order, pretrial, and discovery motions require good-faith conferral and a certificate of conferral under Local Civil Rule 16.1.C.4.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Motions and briefing (trap): A brief must accompany every motion except motions for continuance, extension of time, to compel discovery, or to present an uncontested matter. Responses (with brief) are due 14 days after service, but 28 days for dispositive motions. Replies are allowed as of right only for dispositive motions and motions for injunctive relief (14 days after the response); otherwise only with leave, then due in 7 days. Briefs may not exceed 25 pages without leave. Oral argument only on matters the court selects, usually complex ones. No courtesy copies unless requested. An unexcused failure to file a motion or response on time can lead to summary grant or denial of the motion; noncompliance with the case management order can lead to dismissal or judgment.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Motions must comply with Local Rule 56, with a concise statement of material facts citing the record and an appendix under LR 56.B.3. The counter statement must track the movant’s paragraphs and address every disputed fact; a reply statement is limited to new facts raised by the non-movant. Unsupported propositions may be rejected or the record read as the opponent presents it, and facts not specifically controverted are deemed admitted (LR 56.E).

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Communications and conferences: In urgent situations, letters or phone calls to chambers are allowed (for example, a 1–2 day extension when something unexpected prevents a timely filing), but the judge strongly prefers a docketed motion. Law clerks may be contacted about status. Phone participation in case management and status conferences is allowed mainly for out-of-town counsel. Lead trial counsel must attend conciliation and pretrial settlement conferences in person. Trial counsel must attend all conferences with settlement authority or with principals immediately available by phone; principals are encouraged to attend settlement conferences. At settlement conferences a principal with full authority must appear.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Case management and discovery
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Case management and discovery: Initial case management conference about 60 days after all counsel appear, followed by the case management order and ADR referral order. Discovery is normally 150 days. Pending motions, including motions to dismiss and for summary judgment, do not stay discovery or any other deadline; stays are granted only when grounds are “obvious.” The discovery deadline is extended only with leave, by a motion giving reasons and listing every prior extension; the proposed order must extend all remaining pretrial deadlines. Counsel must confer in good faith on discovery and scheduling disputes. Rule 11 and Rule 37 motions must be briefed and are generally decided at the end of the case; the judge is hesitant to award fees as sanctions.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: Opposing counsel must be identified and contacted; ex parte rulings are extremely rare. The judge prefers a prompt status conference, then schedules a preliminary injunction hearing promptly or as counsel request.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): Pretrial narrative statements must specify all material facts and case-in-chief exhibits; anything not specified may be excluded. Non-jury cases: with its narrative statement, plaintiff files numbered proposed findings and conclusions with record cites and a pretrial brief; defendant’s counter-findings must track plaintiff’s numbering. Revised findings may follow the transcript (plaintiff’s 30 days after the transcript, defendant’s 30 days after plaintiff’s). A pretrial settlement conference follows resolution of dispositive motions, and a Trial Management Order then sets trial deadlines. Challenged deposition designations require a memorandum on admissi

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Trial management order (civil)
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Trial management order (civil): Plaintiff’s exhibits are numbered and defendant’s lettered. Motions in limine briefs are limited to 15 pages; the judge generally rules on them shortly before or at trial. Substantive jury instructions with authority are filed by the set date. Objections must quote the full instruction, identify the objectionable language, cite authority, and offer an alternative; argumentative or formula instructions will not be given. Stipulations cover expert CVs (read into the record if unopposed), facts, exhibits, medical records, expert reports, and a brief statement of claims and defenses for the jury. The jury is 8 persons.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Trial: A firm civil trial date is set after the final pretrial settlement conference, sometimes with an earlier back-up date; other obligations of counsel and witnesses generally won’t move the firm date. Jury trials Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Jurors generally may not take notes. The judge conducts voir dire; counsel may propose added questions by the order’s deadline. Visual aids in opening need all counsel’s consent; an exhibit must generally be offered before substantive testimony about it. Instructions are discussed at an informal charge conference, and formal objections are made after the charge is read. During deliberations, counsel must be able to return within 15 minutes.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Proposed orders on extensions must include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. Special voir dire and points for charge filed after the deadlines in the trial management order are deemed waived absent good cause. No special interrogatories; Apprendi issues are charged as elements. The government is encouraged to disclose Jencks material at least 5 business days before trial. A defendant needs a formal motion for leave to travel outside the district even if the AUSA and probation consent. Sentencing memoranda are optional but must come early enough to be considered.

docs.t: Judge David S. Cercone (W.D. Pa.) — Special case types
docs.x: Judge David S. Cercone, W.D. Pa.. Special case types: Patent cases follow a posted case management order under the Local Patent Rules, with a Rule 16 conference within 30 days after the claim construction ruling and summary judgment motions 30 days after expert depositions close (response 30 days, reply 15, sur-reply 10). The judge uses a standard Social Security order and requires a RICO statement after the initial status conference in RICO cases. Bankruptcy appeals are briefed under Bankruptcy Rule 8009; oral argument only on request.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Motion form and response deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Motion form and response deadlines (trap): Every motion is two documents: the motion and a separate brief. Evidentiary materials go in a separate tabbed document, and a proposed order stating the specific relief must be attached; a response must also attach a proposed order. The opposing party must file a response to every motion, even if it does not oppose; letters are not responses, and failure to respond may be deemed consent. Responses are due 14 days after service for discovery motions, 7 days for motions in limine, 30 days for summary judgment, and 21 days for all other motions.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Page limits and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Page limits and format (trap): Briefs are limited to 10 pages for discovery motions, 5 for motions in limine, 20 (excluding tables) for summary judgment, and 15 for all other motions. Text and footnotes in 12-point font with 1-inch margins; text double-spaced, footnotes may be single-spaced. Evading these limits gets the brief stricken or the excess treated as outside the record without notice. Reply briefs are discouraged and need leave except on summary judgment; they must identify the novel matter warranting reply. Replies and surreplies (also by leave only) are limited to 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: File a separate statement of material facts with numbered paragraphs, each citing the evidence; the opponent files a separate paragraph-by-paragraph response citing and attaching evidence for each disputed fact. The argument must, for each claim, set out its elements with current Third Circuit authority if available. Noncompliance may result in the motion being decided against that party. Oral argument is generally not held on summary judgment, though it is on most other substantive motions, especially motions to dismiss.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Correspondence, chambers, and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Correspondence, chambers, and courtesy copies: Correspondence is disfavored except to report status (e.g., mediation); to get action, file a motion. No letter briefs. Law clerks may be contacted about scheduling and administrative matters only. No courtesy copies unless requested, except evidentiary materials over 25 pages, which should be marked, tabbed, and furnished to chambers. The judge prefers in-person attendance at conferences but allows phone attendance on request for good reason.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions and discovery
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Extensions and discovery: Extension motions must explain why deadlines could not be met (and, for discovery, what remains and how long it will take), and the proposed order must list every affected date. The judge may rule without a response and is stricter as the case advances. Discovery is typically set at 90 to 120 days; if longer is allowed, do not expect an extension. Discovery disputes not requiring review of written responses or a written order are resolved by phone; otherwise file a motion and appear in person. Expert discovery and any Daubert hearing are generally scheduled after fact discovery.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: At least four civil conferences: an initial Rule 16 conference, a close-of-fact-discovery conference (seek any extension before it), a pretrial conference, and a conference on the jury selection date. The judge discusses settlement in jury cases; in nonjury cases only if complex and all parties consent, otherwise referring to an ADR panel lawyer or private mediator. No settlement discussions while a dispositive motion is pending, and none on jury selection day.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Injunctions
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Injunctions: Expedited hearings are scheduled as needed; TROs rarely issue without both parties present, and if the judge is unavailable, the miscellaneous judge hears TRO motions. Proposed findings and conclusions are required in matters decided by the court, except emergency injunctive relief ruled on from the bench.

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Court sits Monday through Thursday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel must be available at 9:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Sidebars are highly disfavored: raise issues at the daily 4:30 p.m. conference, or the objection will generally be resolved in front of the jury. Motions in limine are due by the court-set date or, if none, at least 1 week before trial. Openings and closings are limited to 1 hour per side and may not be split among co-counsel; the jury is charged before closings. Plaintiffs mark exhibits with numbers, defendants with letters; give the court a copy of all exhibits 2 weeks before trial, noting agreed authenticity and admissibility, plus a second set for the record. One attorney per witness; no greeting witnesses, no first names, no pacing. File one combined set of jury instructions marking agreed ones and identifying the profferin

docs.t: Judge Joy Flowers Conti (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Motions must be in writing, and oral argument is generally scheduled. Submit proposed voir dire and jury instructions (joint instructions not required) before the pretrial conference; witness lists and exhibits are exchanged on the first day of trial. Tentative guideline findings generally issue the day before sentencing; PSR objections are resolved at sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Response and reply deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Response and reply deadlines (trap): Responses: 21 days from service for motions to dismiss, 28 days for summary judgment, and 7 days for all other motions unless a specific order says otherwise. No separate briefing order is needed, and a late response may be deemed a concession. Replies without leave: 7 days after service of the response for motions to dismiss and 14 days for summary judgment. Replies on any other motion, and all sur-replies, need leave obtained in advance. The court may decide unopposed motions or those not affecting substantial rights (e.g., withdrawal, setting a conference, most extensions) without waiting for a response.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Page limits and format
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Page limits and format: Briefs on motions to dismiss and summary judgment: 25 pages, excluding tables and exhibits; replies 15 pages. All other motions: 10-page briefs and 10-page replies. 12-point font including footnotes, one-inch margins, double-spaced text (footnotes may be single-spaced). Skip extended recitations of settled standards and keep fact sections non-argumentative with record citations.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Each motion must state whether the movant discussed it with all other parties and their positions. Joint, consented, or uncontested motions must be so titled, and a multi-party motion lacking everyone’s consent must say so on page one. Substantive motions need a separate brief; discovery, extension, and continuance motions generally do not. File a proposed order stating the specific relief as a separate attachment, with both the motion and any response. Cite deposition passages by page and line; the court strongly urges filing non-confidential deposition transcripts in full. Motions to amend must attach a redline of the proposed amended document. Letters to the court are not motions or responses. Flag urgency in the motion; the court may hold a phone conference instead of written responses.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 conferral (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 conferral (trap): Before any Rule 12(b) motion, meet and confer about whether amendment can cure the defect. Every such motion must include a certificate of good-faith conferral.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): Meet and confer before filing to see whether claims or issues can be stipulated away. The movant files its concise statement and sends the opponent a Word copy. The opponent responds paragraph by paragraph within the movant’s document, adds any additional facts at the end, and returns a Word copy; replies to additional facts go in the same document, so one combined statement is filed. The court uses the last-filed version. Don’t duplicate the movant’s exhibits; cite exhibits by ECF number and page where possible.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery and case-management disputes
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Discovery and case-management disputes: After conferring, file a brief joint motion covering the nature and scope of the dispute, each side’s position, counsel’s availability over the next 7 days, and any time sensitivity. docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Extensions: Extension motions need a certificate of conferral stating whether the other side consents and, if it opposes, whether it will respond; any response is due within 7 days of filing. The April 2021 chart instead says to tell the court by telephone immediately; the October 2024 order is newer. Proposed orders must include the new date certain (or a blank for it) and reset every affected deadline.

docs.t: Judge Marilyn Horan (W.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and argument
docs.x: Judge Marilyn Horan, W.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and argument: If a brief with its appendices or exhibits reaches 50 pages, furnish a paper courtesy copy after e-filing so the ECF header appears. No other courtesy copies unless requested. Motions may be decided without oral argument; a party may request it if it will materially help.

docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies (trap): If a brief with its appendices or exhibits reaches 50 pages or more, deliver a paper courtesy copy when filing: 3-hole punched in black binders no thicker than 3 inches, cover and spine labeled with case name, number, subject, ECF document, and filing party. No other courtesy copies unless requested.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery and case management disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Discovery and case management disputes (trap): Lead counsel must confer in person or by phone, agree on the scope of the dispute, and contact the law clerk or courtroom deputy for a telephone conference, usually held immediately or within 24 hours. A conference is required before any motion to compel, for sanctions, or for a non-consensual protective order; skipping it can lead to deferral or denial. If the court sets a phone conference before a response is due, the non-movant need not file a written response. “Sauce for the goose” arguments rarely persuade. Fact discovery is ordinarily 150 days. Discovery extension motions, filed before the deadline, must list discovery done and planned, show good cause, list prior extensions, and attach a proposed order with the new date; a first request is routinely granted.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Communications, extensions, and oral argument
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Communications, extensions, and oral argument: Communicate by motion with a proposed order, not letters; the court dockets any case-related correspondence it receives. Call chambers for emergencies or agreed short extensions; unopposed extensions of 5 days or less may be requested by phone. Staff contacts must state that all parties know and concur. Extension motions should state opposing positions, list prior extensions, come at least 5 business days before the deadline, and give the date certain; if several deadlines move, restate them all. Opponents of short extensions must show actual prejudice. Oral argument is often set on motions that would dispose of a claim or defense, sanctions and disqualification motions, and successive scheduling requests, and the court often rules from the bench.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: Counsel must confer in person or by phone (not email) before any conference so no one is surprised. The attending lawyer, ordinarily lead trial counsel, must know the case well enough to stipulate, argue pending motions, and discuss settlement. Phone conferences are the norm, but settlement conferences, final pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are not ordinarily by phone. For phone conferences, give chambers direct numbers by 4 p.m. the day before (the initial case management order says 48 hours ahead at 412-208-7433). Initial case management conference within 30 days of a responsive pleading or Rule 12 motion; lead counsel needs full settlement authority, and clients and insurers must be reachable by phone. The Rule 26(f) conference must be in person or by phone with all trial counsel; the order includes a Rule 502(d) non

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Sealing and TROs
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Sealing and TROs: Motions to seal must state the specific factual and legal basis, and the proposed order must include the court’s language allowing it to be vacated for cause. TRO and injunction movants must show serious efforts to contact the other side by Rule 65 affidavit or there will be no hearing or TRO. Arrange any bond at filing; motions and responses need affidavits and proposed findings and conclusions, and counsel must be ready to proceed immediately.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Final pretrial conference: all trial lawyers, parties, and insurer representatives with full authority attend in person; motions in limine, instructions, and other issues are argued and generally decided there. In limine briefs are limited to 10 pages. Witness lists with a one-page offer of proof per witness; a Joint Exhibit List Chart filed and a binder of exhibits delivered to chambers; plaintiffs use numbers and defendants letters. One combined set of jury instructions (disputed ones with each side’s authority) with a Word copy; separate sets are not accepted. Bench trials and hearings: plaintiff’s proposed findings and conclusions within 14 days after the close, defendant’s counter-findings 14 days later, each with a brief of up to 20 pages and a Word copy.

docs.t: Judge Mark R. Hornak (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel meet the court at 8:30 a.m., sidebars are disfavored, and issues not raised then are generally decided in open court. The jury is often selected the Wednesday before trial; be in the courtroom by 8:45 a.m. on selection day. Individual voir dire is in chambers with one client representative present. Openings and closings usually 30 minutes per side; in civil trials plaintiff closes last. Co-counsel may not split a witness without advance leave (relaxed for newer lawyers). Next day’s witnesses to opponents by 5 p.m. Exhibits go through the court’s electronic system, which counsel must know how to use. Contact the courtroom deputy (Brian Babik) at least 1 week ahead about trial technology, and give chambers a list of outside devices and who will bring them; Mac users bring their own adapter. docs.x: Judge Mark R. Hornak, W.D. Pa.. Every lawyer must be fully prepared regardless of experience (e.g., thoroughly familiar with the record and law when arguing summary judgment) and have authority matching the proceeding; at a scheduling conference, that ordinarily means full authority to agree to a discovery or trial schedule, argue pending motions, and discuss settlement stat

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap): Before filing any Rule 12 motion, including a Rule 12(c) motion, defense counsel must confer with plaintiff’s counsel on whether the pleading defects can be cured. The motion must include a certificate of good-faith efforts to confer, or it will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Briefing and summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Briefing and summary judgment (trap): Unless ordered otherwise, a principal brief is limited to 20 pages; the court issues briefing schedules for all motions, setting later due dates and page limits. Routine motions (amendment, extensions, continuances) need no brief but must state whether consent was obtained. The court sets a briefing schedule for Rule 56 motions and typically won’t consider motions filed before discovery closes. For most motions it excuses Local Rule 56’s separate concise and responsive statements of fact; cross-motions are briefed like cross-appeals under FRAP 28.1, and complex cases may use issue-specific briefs. Oral argument may be requested on any motion; the judge encourages junior attorneys to argue.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Brief-writing preferences
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Brief-writing preferences: The posted preferences favor short, plain, active-voice briefs with strong topic sentences, a 1–2 page roadmap introduction, and few block quotes, footnotes, or adjectives. Avoid Latin and legalese (including “arguendo,” “infra,” and “supra”), defined terms, and acronyms; use proper names instead of “Plaintiffs” and “Defendants,” and describe opponents respectfully. Cite cases with parentheticals, preferably direct quotations, rather than extended case analysis.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Discovery (trap): No written discovery or other formal discovery before the initial case management conference and the case management order. Propose a realistic discovery deadline: the court dislikes extension motions and is unlikely to grant them, even on consent. For disputes, after conferring, contact chambers; the court typically asks for brief email summaries and then guides, decides, or orders briefing. No discovery motions until after the email exchange, and Rule 37 expenses will be awarded to the prevailing party when permitted.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Initial conference and ADR (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Initial conference and ADR (trap): The Rule 26(f) report uses the judge’s shortened form (fact and expert discovery subjects, deadlines, Rule 502 order, ESI, protective order). The ADR stipulation must set the session within 60 days of the initial case management conference, list attendees by name and title, and include a representative with full settlement authority, or it will be stricken. The conference is usually in person; out-of-town lead counsel may move to appear by phone or video. Be ready for substantive discussion.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Contact, continuances, and court reporters
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Contact, continuances, and court reporters: Contact Courtroom Deputy Peter Kosloski (peter_kosloski@pawd.uscourts.gov, 412-208-7495) for scheduling and to raise discovery disputes; staff give no legal advice. Continuance motions should propose alternative dates near the original date when all counsel are available; good cause includes illness, family emergency, pre-paid vacation, or a prior court proceeding. In civil cases a court reporter is generally present only for arguments on substantive motions, evidentiary hearings, the final pretrial conference, and trial; counsel should request one if they want something on the record.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Trial and presumptive trial dates
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Trial and presumptive trial dates: In certain cases (usually personal-injury, UM/UIM, and non-complex employment and civil rights cases), the court sets a presumptive trial date about 10–18 months after the initial conference; continuances only in extraordinary circumstances. A separate pretrial order sets trial procedures. Counsel stand when speaking for the record and need permission to approach a witness.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Injunctions and class actions
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Injunctions and class actions: For a TRO or preliminary injunction, the court typically schedules a prompt phone conference; serve the defendant, as ex parte motions are rarely granted. Named plaintiffs in class and collective actions must attend all conferences, hearings, settlement conferences, and mediations (in person or remotely); incentive awards require showing active involvement. Expect close scrutiny at preliminary approval. Individual, non-collective FLSA settlements need no court approval; just file a stipulation of dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ranjan (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ranjan, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Initial case conference about 40 days after arraignment; don’t seek to extend the pretrial-motion deadline again until after it. The government should be ready to summarize its evidence and discovery. For a change of plea, the government must email any plea agreement and its summary of trial evidence to defense counsel and the court 7 days before the hearing. The judge does not prefer Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreements; serial extensions of the motions deadline are disfavored absent complexity.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Briefs, page limits, and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Briefs, page limits, and deadlines (trap): Briefs are filed with every motion except discovery, extension, and continuance motions, and are capped at 20 pages; incorporating earlier briefs is prohibited. Double-spaced, at least 12-point font, paginated. Responses: 21 days for dispositive motions and 14 days for non-dispositive motions unless ordered otherwise. The procedures say replies and sur-replies need leave and are capped at 5 pages, but the attached Order on Motions Practice (Exhibit A) allows dispositive replies within 14 days of the response, up to 10 pages, and caps non-dispositive responses at 5 pages; check the order in your case. Reconsideration motions are due within 7 days, with responses 7 days later.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Conferral certificates (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Conferral certificates (trap): Discovery motions, motions in limine, and Rule 12 motions require a certificate of conferral; email exchanges are not enough. Under the standard Rule 12(b) order, parties (including pro se) must confer about whether amendment can cure the defect; motions lacking the certificate are summarily denied, and a nonmovant who fails to engage may face fees, costs, or denial of later leave to amend. Parties should try not to oppose timely early motions to amend.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Communicate with the court only by motion with a proposed order stating the specific relief; no correspondence unless requested. Oral argument only on selected complex matters, by order; the court may open with its tentative ruling and may rule from the bench. No courtesy copies of documents on CM/ECF, but send a courtesy copy of any exhibits or appendices over 20 pages. The form case management and pretrial orders call for courtesy copies of certain filings concurrently with filing.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Position letters and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Position letters and settlement (trap): At least 3 business days before every case management, settlement, or pretrial conference, each party faxes a confidential position letter (facts, strengths and weaknesses, settlement posture) to chambers at (412) 208-7487. Do not file or share it. Chief trial counsel, the client, and any insurer or underwriter with full settlement authority (to policy limits) must attend settlement conferences in person. The settlement conference form order also requires each party to submit a confidential proposed settlement agreement within 2 business days of the conference. Be ready to discuss and agree to an ADR option at the case management and settlement conferences.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Case management and discovery
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Case management and discovery: Initial case management conference within 30 days of a responsive pleading; chief trial counsel and parties with full settlement authority attend. A Rule 502(d) order is available on request; no trial date is set at this stage. Discovery generally runs 150 days, with extensions for cause if counsel advanced the case. The form case management order limits written discovery to 25 interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission, including subparts, and requires periodic joint discovery status reports. Under the form case management order, discovery motion responses are due within 5 days (excluding weekends and holidays), memoranda are capped at 5 pages, and no replies are allowed. Deposition disputes: written motions are discouraged; contact the court jointly through the law clerk at (412) 208-7480.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Strict compliance with Local Rule 56; the argument must cite current Third Circuit authority establishing the elements of each claim. Noncompliance may result in the motion being decided against the party. The court issues a motions order with deadlines. The form case management order sets 20-page memoranda, responses within 30 days, and 10-page replies within 10 days.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions and TROs
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Extensions and TROs: The court is not inclined to grant extensions; requests must be by motion with a proposed order, good cause, and opposing counsel’s position. Postponing court appearances is granted infrequently. For a TRO, show serious efforts to contact the opposing party, supported by a Rule 65(b) affidavit, or no hearing or TRO. Moving and responding papers must include affidavits.

docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Under the form jury pretrial order: witness lists with 1-page offers of proof due 1 month (plaintiff) and 3 weeks (defendant) before trial; designations 2 weeks before, counter-designations 1 week; motions in limine 2 weeks before with responses 10 days before, 5-page briefs; joint stipulations and supplemental voir dire 10 days before. File one unified set of jury instructions marking agreed and disputed instructions; separate sets are not accepted. Trial briefs are capped at 15 pages and most useful at least 14 days before trial. Exhibit binders for the court at least 3 days before trial per the procedures (2 days in the form orders), plus a Joint Exhibit

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Trial runs Monday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel meet with the court at 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Sidebars are highly disfavored; issues not raised at those conferences are generally ruled on in front of the jury. Co-counsel may not split a witness examination or closing. Redirect and recross require leave. About 30 minutes is suggested for opening and closing; witness time limits may be set. docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Pretrial conference about a week before trial. Voir dire questions at least 1 week before trial and motions in limine and jury instructions at least 2 weeks before, unless the pretrial order says otherwise; sidebars are not permitted. Jencks material expected by the final pretrial conference; Brady violations may bring sanctions, suppression, dismissal, or contempt. Travel outside Western Pennsylvania requires a formal motion. The pre-sentence order sets objections, position statements, tentative findings, and a telephonic conference before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Nora Barry Fischer (W.D. Pa.) — Other case types
docs.x: Judge Nora Barry Fischer, W.D. Pa.. Other case types: Bankruptcy appeals: appellant’s brief within 14 days after docketing and appellee’s 14 days later; replies upon notice to the court. RICO plaintiffs must file a RICO Case Statement within 14 days of the complaint. Time limits for class certification and Social Security actions are strictly enforced. Patent cases follow an initial patent scheduling order under the Local Patent Rules.

The opposing party must file a separate response to every motion (with a brief for substantive motions) unless the motion is joint or unopposed. Letters are not motions or responses, and a late response may be deemed a concession. Oral argument is at the court’s discretion; a party may request it.

Discovery generally runs 150 days and is extended for good cause only if counsel advanced the case. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery; phased discovery may be considered.

docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Communications and phone appearances (trap): Communicate by motion, not letters; no correspondence to the judge unless requested. docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Per the Final Scheduling Order form, no briefing beyond the motion and response without leave.
