docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Oral argument: Requests are considered case by case; the court will likely allow argument if an associate or more junior attorney argues.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Deadlines without briefing orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Deadlines without briefing orders (trap): No separate briefing order generally issues, and awaiting one is no excuse. Responses to non-dispositive motions are due in 10 calendar days; responses to Rule 12 motions in 20 calendar days, with replies 5 calendar days later. Summary judgment oppositions are due in 30 calendar days and replies (including responses to new facts in the responsive concise statement) in 14 calendar days. Reconsideration motions are due within 10 calendar days, with responses 10 calendar days later.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions to dismiss (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions to dismiss (trap): Meet and confer before a Rule 12(b) motion about whether amendment can cure the defect (including with pro se parties, but not incarcerated pro se litigants). A motion without a certificate of conferral is summarily denied, and one filed without a brief is summarily dismissed. Briefs are capped at 25 pages; replies allowed without leave for Rule 12(b) and 12(c), capped at 5 pages and limited to new matters. Partial motions to dismiss do not excuse filing an answer. Parties should try not to oppose timely early motions to amend.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Every motion needs a separate proposed order stating the specific relief. Briefs are filed with the motion, except for discovery, extension, and continuance motions. Incorporating earlier briefs is prohibited. Double-spaced, at least 12-point font, paginated. Hyperlinks to CM/ECF filings, exhibits, and Westlaw are strongly encouraged (except for pro se parties); links to sealed documents, other websites, or audio/video are prohibited, and cited websites must be attached as dated PDFs. No paper courtesy copies. Oral argument only on selected complex matters, by order; there is no set motion day. Don’t send correspondence to the judge unless requested. Conferences may be rescheduled by phone to the deputy clerk only with all counsel on the line.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Strict compliance with Local Rule 56. Briefs are capped at 25 pages (excluding exhibits and concise statements) and replies at 5 pages; surreplies only with leave. The argument must cite current Supreme Court and Third Circuit authority establishing the elements of each claim. Responses to the concise statement must reprint each original fact followed by the response, seriatim. Concise statements and responses have no page limit; supporting documents go in an appendix.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes: After conferring, file an extremely brief motion, with no supporting brief and the discovery at issue attached, and call chambers so the deputy can schedule a conference. Noncompliance means denial without prejudice. Discovery motions and motions in limine require a certificate of conferral; email exchanges are not enough. Disputes during depositions may be raised by a joint call. Discovery runs 150 days if the parties choose mediation or early neutral evaluation and 120 days for arbitration. Dispositive motions and ADR do not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR: Requests to participate in a conference by phone must be made by motion more than 2 business days before it, for good cause. Extension and continuance motions must state supporting facts and opposing counsel’s position, suggest alternative dates when all parties are available, and be filed more than 2 business days before the deadline. File an ADR stipulation naming a proposed neutral before the initial case management conference; if the parties can’t agree, the court chooses.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement authority (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Settlement authority (trap): In jury cases, counsel and persons with ultimate settlement authority (including knowledgeable insurer representatives) must attend settlement conferences, including the final pretrial conference, in person. Sanctions may follow if the person present lacks full authority; phone participation only rarely, with prior leave for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Post-discovery status conference after fact discovery; a final status conference after dispositive rulings, preceded by a settlement meet-and-confer. The final pretrial conference is held immediately before trial. Submit a single agreed set of jury instructions and verdict form using Third Circuit model instructions; for disputed ones, each side submits its version with authority. In bench trials, file numbered proposed findings and conclusions and a supporting brief of up to 20 pages within 20 days after trial, plus editable word-processing copies. Submit a joint glossary of technical terms, if needed, 3 business days before trial. Exhibits are marked P and D and listed in the pretrial narrative statements; get approval in advance for demonstratives in opening.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (Erie)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Trial (Erie): Trial generally runs Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The court conducts preliminary voir dire; jurors may take notes. Only one attorney per party may examine a given witness. Tell the court in advance about video testimony (not filed with the clerk) and test it on the court’s equipment at least a week before trial. Counsel must be reachable in person or by phone during deliberations. Notify the court before interviewing jurors.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — R&R objections and TROs
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. R&R objections and TROs: Objection briefs of 10 pages or less are encouraged. New authority or evidence not given to the magistrate judge will not be considered without a reason for the omission. No TRO if the other side has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service can’t be made, or if it lacks a Rule 65(b)(1)(A) affidavit or verified complaint. Support and responses must include affidavits.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Certificate of conferral (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Certificate of conferral (trap): Every motion must attach, as a separate exhibit, a Certificate of Conferral detailing the efforts to resolve the matter and stating whether each other party consents or opposes and whether it will file a response. A missing certificate can get the motion stricken or summarily denied, with possible sanctions. Conferral must include a verbal discussion (phone, video, or in person) on the merits; exchanging emails or letters, or leaving a voicemail the evening before or the day of filing, does not count. Counsel must also confer verbally before any conference with the court so that no one is surprised by another party’s position.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): Motions must state the specific relief and its factual and legal grounds, with a proposed order filed as a separate attachment stating the specific relief (not “the motion is granted”). Communicate with the court by motion, not email or letter, unless asked. No brief is needed for discovery motions or extension or continuance motions. Dispositive and class certification briefs: 25 pages (replies 15). All other motion briefs: 10 pages (replies 5). Any other written submission: 5 pages. Overlong filings may be stricken. No courtesy copies of anything on CM/ECF unless requested. Oral argument at the court’s discretion; a request should briefly explain why argument would help.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Response deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Response deadlines (trap): Responses: 21 days for motions to dismiss and to compel arbitration; 30 days for summary judgment and class certification; 5 days for discovery and case management motions (such as extensions or rescheduling); 7 days for all other motions. The 2026 version shortens the general deadline from 21 days in the 2021 version. Replies without leave within 7 days of the response (14 days for summary judgment and class certification). Sur-replies are disfavored and need leave. Motions for reconsideration are due within 7 days of the order. For urgent motions, say so in the motion and phone chambers and all counsel. Stipulations to change response times are not a substitute for a motion and court approval.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion may be filed until Judge Hardy holds an informal phone conference and grants leave. After conferring in good faith, the parties jointly contact Courtroom Deputy Kallie Sheets (412-208-7570, Kallie_sheets@pawd.uscourts.gov) with a jointly proposed agenda that fairly identifies the disputed issues. If leave is granted, the response is due within 5 days, replies are typically not permitted, and rulings often come within 7 days. During depositions, the attorneys together may call to see if the court will resolve a dispute then. Discovery ordinarily runs 150 days; any variance must be raised in the Rule 26(f) report and at the initial conference. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Extensions (trap): Extension motions must state all opposing counsel’s positions (and whether they will oppose in writing), list prior extensions, attach a proposed order and Certificate of Conferral, and be titled (with matching docket text) like “[First] Motion for [Un/Contested] Extension of Discovery” or “[First] Motion to Modify Case Management Order.” File at least 5 business days before the deadline when practicable. A first reasonable discovery extension is routinely granted if the motion describes discovery done to date and the specific discovery planned, with a tentative schedule. Don’t assume joint requests will be granted, especially late ones, and don’t informally agree to work “out of time” without a court order.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and ADR
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and ADR: The court prefers in-person proceedings. Initial case management and routine civil status conferences are usually by phone; settlement conferences, pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are in person unless permitted otherwise. Before the initial conference (usually set within 30 days after an answer), file the Rule 26(f) report and a complete Stipulation Selecting ADR Process naming the ADR type, the neutral, a confirmed session date within 60 days of the conference, and all attendees (including a representative with settlement authority). Incomplete filings may be stricken. Lead trial counsel, familiar with the case and able to stipulate, ordinarily attends conferences ready to argue pending motions and discuss settlement. A post-fact discovery status conference is usually held within 30 days after discovery closes; chambers may e

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Leave is required for each document to be sealed. A party filing material it or another party wants sealed must first move for leave to file provisionally under seal after conferral, stating each party’s position; any party wanting the material kept sealed must then justify it item by item under In re Avandia (3d Cir. 2019). Stipulated protective orders must include the court’s required sealing provision, and the proposed sealing order must include language allowing it to be vacated for cause. Redacting personal identifiers under LR 5.2 needs no leave.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: The movant must show by Rule 65(b) affidavit serious efforts to contact the other side and why notice should not be required, or there will be no hearing or TRO. Have any bond arranged at filing. Motions and responses need supporting affidavits and proposed findings and conclusions on the court’s schedule. Be ready to proceed immediately and to choose a neutral for expedited ADR before a preliminary injunction hearing.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Settlement: In jury cases the court may require confidential position letters (salient facts, strengths and weaknesses, settlement posture), emailed to chambers and not filed or shared. A judicial settlement conference order typically requires an exchange of written demand and offer, a joint proposed settlement agreement with a statement of key disagreements, and ex parte position letters.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Before seeking more time for pretrial motions, confer and state whether the government consents; include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. A pre-plea presentence report requires the defendant’s written consent and Rule 32(e)(1) waiver in the form set out in the procedures. Travel motions must state the positions of the government and Probation/Pretrial Services. After pretrial motions are decided, defense counsel should be ready to tell the court at a status conference whether the defendant will plead or go to trial.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Communications with chambers: Communicate with the court by motion with a proposed order; no correspondence unless the court requests or approves it. Administrative (not merits) questions, including status inquiries, may go, preferably by email, to Deputy Clerk Elizabeth Abbott (Elizabeth_Abbott@pawd.uscourts.gov) or Career Law Clerk Rebecca Good McBride (Rebecca_McBride@pawd.uscourts.gov). Scheduling emails go to the deputy clerk. Emergency or time-sensitive filings: email electronic courtesy copies to both the career law clerk and the deputy clerk immediately after filing on CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): A motion must state in short and plain form the specific relief, the factual and legal grounds, and whether it was discussed with all other parties and their positions. Attach only the evidentiary materials necessary to decide it, plainly marked. File a proposed order stating the specific relief as a separate attachment; “the motion is granted” orders are not sufficient. For routine motions (leave to amend, extensions, continuances), confer to seek consent and state whether consent was obtained.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Briefs and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Briefs and page limits (trap): No briefs on motions for extension of time or continuance, and none on discovery disputes unless the court directs after a telephonic status conference. Dispositive motions: principal and opposition briefs 20 pages (excluding tables), replies 15. All other motions: 10 pages, replies 5, absent leave.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Oral argument: Motions are decided with or without argument at the court’s discretion. A party wanting argument must meet and confer, then the parties may file a joint motion explaining why argument would help.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): After a good-faith conference fails, the parties jointly email the deputy clerk to schedule a telephonic status conference. No discovery motions until after that conference, except emergencies certified by counsel. No court reporter unless requested.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Case management conferences
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Case management conferences: The telephonic Initial Case Management Conference is generally set after the answer. Before it, file the Rule 26(f) report and a fully completed Stipulation Selecting ADR Process; failure may lead the court to strike the 26(f) report. Be ready for substantive discussion; off the record unless a reporter is requested. A post-discovery status conference is held no more than 30 days after discovery closes to set summary judgment deadlines or a trial date, followed by a Pretrial Order. A final pretrial/settlement conference precedes trial; all participating trial counsel must attend.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial runs Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with a conference with counsel at 8:00 a.m. on evidentiary issues; counsel must notify all parties of the need for one. The court will not delay trial for last-minute conference requests that could have been raised at the morning conference. Jurors may take notes on court-provided paper and get the final instructions and admitted exhibits during deliberations. Counsel may leave the courthouse during deliberations but must be reachable by phone and able to return within ten minutes.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: No special rules on guilty pleas or plea-agreement deadlines; early plea discussions encouraged. Before seeking more time for pretrial motions, confer for consent, state the result, and include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. Pretrial motions are decided with or without a hearing; note in the motion if a hearing would help. Two formal pretrial conferences once trial is set; the civil trial procedures apply. No separate hearing on PSR objections unless requested. Tentative findings on disputed guideline issues are provided before sentencing, and notice is given of any departure ground not already identified, but the court will not reveal its position on a requested variance in advance.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motions (motions to compel, for protective order, or for sanctions) without the court’s prior permission. First confer by telephone or in person; letters, emails, or faxes do not satisfy the duty unless repeated attempts to talk fail because of the adversary’s conduct. If unresolved, e-file a Consolidated/Joint Discovery Statement: 6 pages for 4 or fewer issues, 10 pages for 5–10 issues, 12 pages for more than 10. For each issue, give Party A’s position, Party B’s response, and Party A’s reply. Attach only an excerpt of the specific disputed requests (and, if needed, responses), not the entire set; no other exhibits without permission. The court decides on the papers or sets a conference, which is recorded by a court reporter. Boilerplate objections (privilege, work product, overbroad, unduly burdensome, irrelevant)

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Record citations must appear in the brief itself, not just in the statement of facts, and each must be followed immediately by the paragraph number of the corresponding statement of fact; deposition cites need page and line. File the complete transcript of each deposition cited in the brief as a separate docket entry. Do not file the original or deliver paper copies to chambers. In responding to a statement of material facts, copy each numbered statement into the response and answer immediately below it. File in text-searchable PDF; nonconforming statements may be returned for revision.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions, page limits, and proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Extensions, page limits, and proposed orders (trap): Extensions require a motion; even joint, unopposed, or consent motions are not granted as a matter of course. Explain with specificity the unforeseen circumstances, give a timetable for finishing, state whether opposing counsel consents, and attach a proposed order. Motions to exceed page limits must be filed at least 5 days before the filing deadline. One filed with the brief will be denied absent a compelling and unanticipated reason, and arguments in excess pages will not be considered. Consent, unopposed, and joint motions must attach a proposed order granting the motion as an exhibit. Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R, and responses, are limited to 15 pages absent permission and must follow LR 5.1 formatting.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Oral argument: Motions are usually decided without argument. A request must state why argument would help and which issues it would address. The court will consider granting argument on a contested, substantive motion if an attorney less than 5 years out of law school will argue at least one substantial issue.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies: Courtroom Deputy Clerk Michelle Beck (404-215-1524, Michelle_Beck@gand.uscourts.gov) is the point of contact; calls may take up to 24 hours to return. Do not discuss the merits with the deputy or law clerks, and make all requests for court action by motion, not letter (LR 7.4). No paper courtesy copies, except for emergency motions under LR 7.2(B). Leaves of absence must be e-filed, not mailed or delivered to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Sealing and TROs
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Sealing and TROs: The court generally seals only items listed in Standing Order 04-02 and will not allow sealed filings without a court order, even on consent. Follow Section II(J) of Appendix H to the Civil Local Rules. TRO and preliminary-injunction requests must be made by separate motion under Rule 65; a request only in the complaint is not considered until the merits. After filing, contact the deputy to request expedited consideration, or the motion is treated as non-emergency.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial conference and motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial conference and motions in limine: Counsel (not parties) attend a pretrial conference, usually within 2 weeks before trial. Plaintiff’s counsel must arrange a meeting at least 10 days before it to discuss settlement and stipulate to facts and issues. Motions in limine are due 21 days before the pretrial conference, responses 9 days after the motion, and replies 5 days after the response; the court usually hears them after the pretrial conference. Be ready to identify case-in-chief witnesses. Number exhibits separately and sequentially; do not group them by category (e.g., “hospital records”).

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Jury selection and charge
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Jury selection and charge: Voir dire questions are filed as the pretrial order directs (LR 16.4). The court asks qualifying questions, jurors answer a printed background questionnaire aloud, and counsel then ask approved questions; cause challenges are heard after all questioning, followed by a 15-minute break before strikes. Civil juries: 8 jurors for trials of a week or less, more for longer trials, and no alternates. Requests to charge are due by 9:00 a.m. on the first day of trial, with a Word version emailed to the deputy the same day. Use Eleventh Circuit Pattern Instructions, then O’Malley (5th ed.), and state pattern instructions for state law; one numbered request per page with authority at the bottom, covering all substantive law.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Trial logistics
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Trial logistics: Ask permission before approaching a witness or the bench. Bringing exhibits boxes, laptops, projectors, or other trial equipment into the courthouse requires a court order; file a motion with proposed order at least 3 business days before the hearing or trial. Contact the deputy to test courtroom technology.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes (trap): Do not file a motion to compel, to quash, for protective order, or for sanctions without a prior conference with the court. After conferring in good faith, the movant emails Courtroom Deputy Brittany Poley (copying all counsel) a one-page summary of the dispute and relief sought, flagging any urgency, and quoting the disputed interrogatory or request. The deputy sets the briefing method (generally short emailed statements) and, if helpful, a conference recorded by a court reporter. Non-party disputes (e.g., subpoenas) follow the same procedure, and the party must tell the non-party about it. During depositions, call the court (404-215-1514 or 404-215-1510) for disputes the parties cannot resolve; for obstruction or Rule 30(d) issues, promptly set up a conference call rather than a later motion.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery responses (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Discovery responses (trap): No “Preamble” or “General Objections” sections; the court disregards them. Each request must get only the specific objections that actually apply. A party that objects and then responds must say whether the response is complete; “subject to and without waiving” answers are not allowed without that statement. Initial disclosures may not be reserved for later supplementation. Serve discovery early enough that responses are due within the discovery period; evidence requested and not produced in discovery is excluded at trial. Produce documents Bates-numbered and labeled by request or in a format showing which request each answers. Privilege claims need particulars (date, author, recipients, subject, purpose).

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions, page limits, and stipulations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Extensions, page limits, and stipulations (trap): Parties may not stipulate to extensions of time or extra pages; a motion is required. Even joint or consent extension motions are not granted as a matter of course and must explain the unforeseen circumstances, give a timetable, state opposing counsel’s position, and attach a proposed order. Motions to exceed page limits are due at least 5 days before the filing deadline; one filed with the brief is denied absent a compelling, unanticipated reason, and excess pages are not considered. Discovery extension motions must be filed before the period ends and state the original and current dates, the number of prior requests and their outcomes, and the adversary’s position (LR 26.2B). Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R, and responses, are limited to 15 pages.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Briefs and filings
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Briefs and filings: Citations go in the text in Bluebook Bluepages form, not in footnotes or endnotes. Title briefs on CM/ECF as “Brief in Support of [motion],” “[Respondent]’s Response in Opposition to [motion],” and “Reply in Support of [motion].” Surreplies are not filed in the normal course. Label uploaded exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. A: Smith Deposition”). Consent, unopposed, and joint motions must include a proposed order. Courtesy copies are not required; if sent, they must bear the CM/ECF header. Leaves of absence must be e-filed, not sent to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Record citations belong in the brief, not just the statement of facts. Cite previously docketed documents by docket number and the ECF-stamped page (e.g., “Dkt. No. [100] at 20”); deposition cites need page and line. Attach only the cited deposition pages to the brief; file the full transcript separately under a notice of filing original deposition transcript. Responses to a statement of material facts must copy each numbered statement and answer immediately below it; a reply to additional facts must copy the original statement and the response. File in text-searchable PDF; nonconforming statements are returned for revision.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Oral argument: Motions are usually decided without argument (LR 7.1(E)); a request must state why argument would help and which issues it would address. The court will grant argument on a contested substantive motion if a lawyer less than 5 years out of law school will conduct the argument (or a large majority of it).

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): The court disfavors broad consent confidentiality orders and will not approve ones that conflict with its sealing views. Material is ordinarily confidential only if it is a trade secret, personal identifying information, or HIPAA-protected health information; over-designation can draw sanctions. Any proposed protective order must include the court’s required provision that confidential material filed or used at a hearing or trial keeps protection only by complying with the Procedures for Electronic Filing Under Seal in Civil Cases. Outside hearings and trial, the court generally seals only items listed in Standing Order 04-02. Consult the designating party first about less restrictive measures, seal or redact only specific portions, and expect material used in open court not to be sealed absent extraordinary circumst

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Contact, scheduling, and TROs
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Contact, scheduling, and TROs: Contact Courtroom Deputy Brittany Poley by email (Brittany_Poley@gand.uscourts.gov) or in writing; phone 404-215-1514, but calls may take 24 hours to return. Do not discuss the merits with the deputy or law clerks. The proposed scheduling order with the Joint Preliminary Report must give specific dates for the end of discovery, dispositive motions, and the pretrial order. A Rule 16 conference is typically set if any party asks, and parties may request other conferences through the deputy. TRO and preliminary-injunction requests require a separate motion (one only in the complaint is not considered); after filing, contact the deputy to request expedited consideration. Pro hac vice lead counsel’s local counsel must know the case and may be called on to attend hearings.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial (trap): Motions in limine are due at least 14 days before the pretrial conference and oppositions at least 7 days before, as a consolidated pleading. Plaintiff’s counsel must arrange a meeting at least 10 days before the conference to discuss settlement and stipulations. Daubert motions are due no later than the date the proposed pretrial order is submitted (LR 26.2C); oppositions within 14 days, replies 7 days after that. Bring the proposed pretrial order, attachments, and any outstanding motions to the conference. Proposed findings and conclusions must be a single unified document (agreed findings first, then disputed ones with proponent, basis, and objection), with a Word copy emailed to the deputy.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Jury trial
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Jury trial: Court usually sits 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with the court expecting 5–6 hours of testimony a day; raise matters outside the jury’s presence at breaks or before the day starts, and have enough witnesses on hand. Voir dire questions are filed with the pretrial order (LR 16.4(B)); jurors answer a printed questionnaire (Exhibit A to the order), counsel ask approved questions, and cause challenges follow, then a 15-minute break before strikes. Civil juries: 8 jurors for trials of a week or less. Requests to charge and verdict forms are due on CM/ECF by noon on the Friday before the trial calendar (LR 51.1(A)), as a single unified set (agreed, then disputed with proponent and basis), with a Word copy emailed to the deputy. docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Discovery (trap): Boilerplate and general objections are prohibited and will be disregarded; object specifically to each request. A party that objects and then responds must say whether anything was withheld because of the objection (“subject to and without waiving” alone is not allowed). Serve requests so responses are due by the close of discovery; the court typically will not compel late-served requests. Identify experts early enough to be deposed within the period. Before any discovery motion, confer in good faith, then contact Ms. Lundy; ordinarily each side submits a 1–2 page letter, and the court rules on the letters, holds a call, or authorizes a motion. The court is usually available by phone for deposition disputes.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): The court disfavors consent confidentiality orders; ordinarily only trade secrets, personal identifying information, and HIPAA-protected health information are truly confidential. Any such order must include (and is deemed to include) the standing order’s language that confidential material submitted to the court keeps its status only by court order. To seal, e-file a motion listing the documents with a proposed order and provisionally file the documents under seal per Appendix H; send no paper copies. Tangible items go to Ms. Lundy in chambers with a proposed order.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Motions practice and filing format
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Motions practice and filing format: Title briefs “Brief in Support of [motion],” “[Respondent]’s Response in Opposition to [motion],” and “Reply in Support of [motion]”; surreplies only if authorized. Label uploaded exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. A: Smith Deposition”). TRO and preliminary injunction requests must be by separate motion (not in the complaint); then contact Ms. Lundy for expedited consideration or a hearing. File leaves of absence on the docket only; they are not automatically granted. Request a conference with the court through Ms. Lundy when counsel has specific goals and an agenda.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial (trap): If a summary judgment motion is pending, the consolidated pretrial order is ordinarily due 30 days after the ruling unless a date is set. Plaintiffs cannot enlarge or change their claims in the pretrial order over objection. Witness and exhibit lists cannot reserve a right to supplement or adopt another party’s list; unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent manifest injustice. Motions in limine and Daubert motions at least 14 days before the pretrial conference, responses 7 days before. Proposed findings and conclusions must also be sent to the law clerk in text-searchable PDF. Anyone without a blue attorney ID card needs a proposed order, at least 3 business days ahead, to bring laptops or camera phones into the courthouse.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Jury selection: Civil trials up to 2 weeks normally seat 8 jurors with no alternates (possibly 7 for trials under a week) from a panel of 20; alert the court promptly if a larger panel is needed, such as for media attention or a mutual insurer. After the court’s qualifying questions, counsel conduct general voir dire of the panel and then question each juror individually. Cause motions follow outside the jury’s presence; each side gets 3 peremptory strikes, alternating on a strike sheet starting with plaintiff.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Trial: Court usually sits 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; counsel present at 9:00 a.m. Expect 5 to 6 hours of testimony per day. Openings are generally limited to 20 minutes and closings to 30 minutes per side; seek more time at the pretrial conference. Before trial, give the deputy a notebook of pre-marked exhibits for the judge and file witness and numbered exhibit lists; hand the court small copies of enlarged boards. No permission is needed to approach a witness with an exhibit. Only the examining attorney may object, stating only the legal basis; one attorney per party at the charge conference. Speak from a microphone; no motions in the jury’s presence, though mistrial motions must be made immediately.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Jury charges
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Jury charges: File, and email to the deputy in Word, a single unified set of proposed instructions no later than the morning of the first day of trial, showing for disputed charges the proponent, the legal basis, and the opposition’s basis. Supplemental charges require oral leave and are not accepted later than a day before the end of trial absent manifest justice.

docs.t: Judge Amy M. Baggio (D. Or.) — Protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Protective orders (trap): Use Judge Baggio’s own modified Tier 2 stipulated protective order template, not the district’s model. Designation disputes go first to conferral, then by email to the courtroom deputy with a one-page letter per party; the court decides whether a motion is needed. A non-designating party files designated material under seal; if it asks in writing to unseal, the designating party has 10 calendar days to move to keep it sealed or the court unseals it.

docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Criminal cases: Motions to continue trial are due 4 weeks before trial. Contact the deputy at least 6 weeks before trial so a jury can be summoned. docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Scheduling
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Scheduling: Rule 16 conferences are set after all defendants answer. Confer on a discovery plan beforehand and have calendars available for discovery and dispositive motion deadlines. After dispositive motions are resolved (or if none are filed), a trial scheduling conference aims to set trial within 120 days. If the parties agree to an expedited schedule, the court will hold a case management conference on limiting discovery and dispositive motions and try to set trial within 6 months.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Trial management order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Trial management order deadlines: The court automatically enters a Trial Management Order 90 days before trial. Pretrial conferences are in person in Eugene. Under the sample TMO: 30 days before the pretrial conference, plaintiff’s exhibit lists and judge’s copies, witness statements and expert reports, special damages, and the pretrial order; 21 days before, defendant’s exhibits and witness materials, deposition designations, trial memoranda, voir dire, and verdict forms; 14 days before, motions in limine, rebuttal materials, and objections; 7 days before, responses. Trial memoranda are limited to 35 pages; all motions in limine and all responses each go in a single document not exceeding 35 pages, with separate motions as subparts.

docs.x: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner, M.D. Ga.. Criminal voir dire: Fill-ins cover the defendant, defense counsel and firm, and the assigned Assistant U.S. Attorney. The court instructs that the defendant need not prove innocence, produce evidence, or testify, and asks whether any juror could not follow that instruction.

docs.t: Judge Robert D. Mariani (M.D. Pa.) — Pretrial submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert D. Mariani, M.D. Pa.. Pretrial submissions (trap): All counsel must submit trial briefs at the pretrial conference, covering all legal issues reasonably anticipated to arise. Pre-mark all exhibits, including demonstrative and photographic evidence, and discuss and exchange them before the final pretrial conference; disagreements are taken up there. A party offering more than 20 written exhibits must provide two copies in loose-leaf binders and one electronic copy for the Jury Evidence Recording System. Proposed jury instructions follow the Local Rules but must be submitted in a digital non-PDF format. Proposed verdict forms are encouraged before the close of trial; the court may use its own.

docs.t: Judge Robert D. Mariani (M.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Robert D. Mariani, M.D. Pa.. Trial: Voir dire is generally conducted by counsel in civil cases and by the judge in criminal cases, subject to change case by case. More than one attorney may participate, but only one may examine a given witness.

docs.t: Judge Robert D. Mariani (M.D. Pa.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Robert D. Mariani, M.D. Pa.. Settlement: The judge pursues settlement thoroughly but refers all settlement discussions in non-jury cases to a magistrate judge or mediator.

docs.t: Judge Yvette Kane (M.D. Pa.) — Correspondence
docs.x: Judge Yvette Kane, M.D. Pa.. Correspondence: Communicate with the court by formal motion. The page excepts discovery disputes but does not state the procedure; call chambers at (717) 221-3990.

docs.t: Judge Yvette Kane (M.D. Pa.) — Conferences
docs.x: Judge Yvette Kane, M.D. Pa.. Conferences: Initial case management conferences are by telephone; status and discovery conferences are by telephone in most cases. Pretrial and settlement conferences are in person.

docs.t: Judge Yvette Kane (M.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies

docs.t: Judge Yvette Kane (M.D. Pa.) — Contact

docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Johnson U.S. Courthouse Complex, 1 Church Street, Montgomery, AL 36104, by hand or mail. Copies must be double-sided and bound in a three-ring binder or large clip. Every proposed order must be filed in CM/ECF as a separate sub-document and emailed in Word to lewischambers@almd.uscourts.gov, copying opposing counsel. Discovery-related proposed orders (HIPAA, protective, confidentiality) go to the assigned magistrate judge’s email instead. All emails to chambers must copy opposing counsel (or, for a pro se party without email, certify mailing to the party’s address).

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Motion format and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Motion format and page limits (trap): Times New Roman 14-point, footnotes 12-point; double-spaced (footnotes and indented quotations may be single-spaced); one-inch margins. Nonconforming motions and briefs may be stricken. Non-summary-judgment motions (motion plus any separate brief) are capped at 15 pages; responses are due within 14 days and capped at 15 pages; replies within 7 days, capped at 10 pages. No sur-replies without leave; the court may rule before responses are filed. No arguments incorporated by reference and no substantive arguments in footnotes. Cite the record by CM/ECF document and page number. Each exhibit must be its own CM/ECF sub-document (e.g., Doc. 12-1). Title and caption must say “Opposed” or “Unopposed,” and the first paragraph must summarize efforts to resolve the issue (not required for motions to dismiss or remand, summary judgm

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Oral argument: Request oral argument on the first page of the motion, brief, or opposition, directly below the case number in the caption. In deciding whether to hear argument, the court considers whether an attorney with fewer than seven years of experience will argue; if so, extra time is given for a more experienced attorney to supplement. No inference is drawn from a decision not to use a newer attorney.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Summary judgment (trap): Opening and response briefs are limited to 35 pages, replies to 15, with a table of contents (not counted). Responses are due 21 days after the motion and replies 14 days after the response; these deadlines apply to all dispositive motions without separate briefing orders. The brief must contain a statement of undisputed facts in simple declarative sentences, each cited to CM/ECF document and page; the opponent must state disputes, additional undisputed facts, and disputed facts. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. File evidentiary submissions separately and before the brief, with a table of contents and numbered exhibits; submit entire depositions with exhibits in four-page-per-sheet form. Email the brief in Word to chambers when filing. Expect to be ordered to mediation before dispositive motions are submitted.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Extensions
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Extensions: Motions to extend any deadline must be filed at least three days before it or will ordinarily be denied automatically; successive requests are strongly disfavored. Extensions of the discovery or dispositive-motion deadline require extraordinary cause. Every extension request must be in writing and state that all counsel were timely contacted and whether they agree; noncompliant or “eleventh hour” requests are denied outright. Discovery-extension motions must list discovery already done (with dates and deponents) and what remains. Parties may adjust expert deadlines by agreement without leave if the discovery cutoff and dispositive-motion deadline are unaffected.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Rule 26(f) and early case management
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Rule 26(f) and early case management: Hold the Rule 26(f) conference within the period set in the Initial Order (typically 21 days); if the parties cannot agree, they meet at 10:00 a.m. at the courthouse on the last Friday of the period. File the joint report within 14 days, starting with a synopsis of no more than one page and ending with the Appendix I scheduling worksheet. Plan for trial within 12 months of service of the complaint; longer schedules need specific justification. Discovery may begin once the report is filed. A party seeking protected health information must present a HIPAA authorization at the planning meeting. In EEOC-charge cases, the plaintiff files the charges and the EEOC response, including the right-to-sue notice, with the initial disclosures.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Amended pleadings, sealing, and withdrawal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Amended pleadings, sealing, and withdrawal (trap): Every amended or proposed amended pleading must include a redline against the original, filed as the final attachment to the pleading or motion for leave. Motions to seal must meet Romero v. Drummond Co., 480 F.3d 1234 (11th Cir. 2007), or will be routinely denied. Counsel may withdraw only by motion stating grounds; counsel for a corporation or LLC cannot withdraw until substitute counsel appears.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Mediation and settlement
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Mediation and settlement: Under the template Scheduling Order, counsel hold a telephone settlement conference (typically 30 days before the dispositive-motion deadline), then within 7 days file a joint status report choosing a private mediator (name and date) or a magistrate judge (four agreed dates). Mediation should occur within 45 days and is treated as mandatory absent good cause. Lead counsel and a representative with full settlement authority must attend; a joint report on the outcome is due within 7 days after mediation.

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. Pretrial and trial: The pretrial conference is held by videoconference at 9:00 a.m. (typically 45–60 days before trial). The plaintiff emails the joint proposed pretrial order in Word to chambers 7 days before it, following the posted template. Witness lists, deposition designations (page and line; no entire depositions), and exhibit lists are typically due 42 days before trial, with objections 28 days and responses 21 days before trial. A PDF of all pre-marked trial exhibits (with photos of physical exhibits) must be emailed to chambers by the exhibit deadline. Voir dire questions, fully briefed motions in limine, and jury instructions are typically due 30 days before trial, with MIL objections 21 days before; avoid duplicating the court’s jury questionnaire and posted voir dire script. Trial terms last two weeks and “trial date” means jury selection. Option

docs.t: Judge Bill Lewis (M.D. Ala.) — AI and attorney fees
docs.x: Judge Bill Lewis, M.D. Ala.. AI and attorney fees: AI tools are permitted but require close supervision and citation-checking; anyone who discovers fabricated citations must raise it immediately, and presenting false citations draws sanctions, including striking the filing. Parties expecting to seek statutory fees must keep contemporaneous time records to the nearest 0.1 hour with specific descriptions, review them monthly, and certify this in any fee petition.

docs.t: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate (M.D. Ala.) — Uniform scheduling order: how deadlines are computed (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate, M.D. Ala.. Uniform scheduling order: how deadlines are computed (trap): Trial and pretrial conference dates are set by the court calendar, and the other civil deadlines count backward from them: proposed pretrial order 1 week before the pretrial conference; dispositive motions 120 days before the pretrial conference; discovery/settlement conference 30 days before the dispositive motion deadline. Plaintiff’s expert witnesses are due 90 days, and defendant’s 60 days, before the discovery cutoff. Pleadings may be amended within 77 days (generally) from the date of the uniform scheduling order.

docs.t: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate (M.D. Ala.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate, M.D. Ala.. Pretrial filings: Witness lists, deposition designations, and exhibits are due 42 days before trial; objections 14 days after the designations; replies to objections 7 days after the objections. Voir dire and motions in limine are also due 42 days before trial, with objections and responses 7 days after.

docs.t: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate (M.D. Ala.) — Chambers contact
docs.x: Judge Kelly Fitzgerald Pate, M.D. Ala.. Chambers contact: Courtroom 5A; chambers (334) 954-3730, patechambers@almd.uscourts.gov; courtroom deputy Kelli Fuller, (334) 954-3973. The page notes judges cannot respond to letters, emails, or other communications about pending cases.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Proposed orders and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Proposed orders and courtesy copies: Submit every proposed order both as a PDF attachment to the motion and in Word by email to huffakerchambers@almd.uscourts.gov, copying all counsel. Johnson, Jr. U.S. Courthouse, One Church St., Montgomery.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Motion briefing and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Motion briefing and page limits (trap): Dispositive and substantive motions (including motions to remand, to dismiss, for summary judgment, and Daubert motions): opening and opposition briefs are capped at 35 double-spaced pages and replies at 15 without advance permission. Responses are due 21 days after the motion and replies 14 days after the response; the motion is then taken under submission without notice. Non-dispositive motions: confer in good faith first, state “opposed” or “unopposed” in the caption, and summarize the conferral and areas of agreement in the first paragraph (failure is grounds for denial). Responses within 14 days, replies within 7. All submissions in 14-point Times New Roman (footnotes 12-point). Briefs over 35 pages need a table of contents, table of authorities, and delineated sections. No “letter briefs” or “letter re

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Summary judgment: Every discussion of evidence must cite page and line of the supporting deposition or document, or the point may be deemed abandoned; failing to address an argument may also be treated as abandonment. File the brief and all supporting evidence with the motion. Opponents are strongly encouraged to concede claims and arguments where appropriate.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Hearings and filing cutoff (trap)
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Hearings and filing cutoff (trap): Unless an order says otherwise, all motions, briefs, and memoranda for a matter set for hearing must be e-filed by 2:00 p.m. CST the day before the hearing, or they will not be considered absent exceptional cause. The court often sets telephone conferences sua sponte; call in at least 5 minutes early. Motions to reschedule require contacting opposing counsel and good cause. Notify the court at least one day ahead if a hearing or sentencing will exceed 45 minutes.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Extensions and discovery
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Extensions and discovery: Extension requests must be in writing, filed well before the deadline, and state that all counsel were timely contacted and whether they agree; noncompliant, oral, or “eleventh hour” requests are denied outright. Discovery-extension motions must list remaining discovery and discovery already done (dates served and answered, depositions taken with deponent names, and depositions requested); lack of progress may defeat the motion. The assigned magistrate judge generally handles discovery motions.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Scheduling
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Scheduling: File the joint Rule 26(f) report within 30 days after all answers are filed unless the court sets another date; review the practices document and template scheduling order first. Any scheduling conference may be attended by phone. Cases are ordinarily set for a civil trial term 18 to 24 months after filing, with the pretrial conference about 28 days before the term. Per the uniform date sheets, dispositive motions are due 180 days before the pretrial conference, the discovery/settlement-conference deadline is 30 days before that, plaintiff’s experts 90 days before the discovery cutoff, and defendant’s experts 28 days after plaintiff’s. Objections to the scheduling order’s deadlines are due within 14 days of the order. Daubert motions are due with dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Mediation and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Mediation and settlement (trap): Counsel must hold a settlement conference by the set deadline, then within 7 days file a joint status report choosing a private mediator (name and date) or a magistrate judge (four agreed dates); mediate within 45 days. Mediation is treated as mandatory absent good cause. The practices document calls this a face-to-face conference, while the template scheduling order calls for a telephone conference. Lead counsel and a representative with full settlement authority must attend mediation; report the result within 7 days. Promptly notify the court of any settlement.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Pretrial: Pretrial conferences are held in Courtroom 2D, Montgomery, absent order and good cause. The plaintiff emails the joint proposed pretrial order in Word to chambers 7 days before the conference. Witness lists, deposition designations (page and line; no entire depositions), and exhibit lists are due 30 days before the pretrial conference, objections 21 days before it, and replies 7 days after objections. Voir dire questions, fully briefed motions in limine, and jury instructions are due 30 days before trial; responses to motions in limine 21 days before. Avoid duplicating the district’s jury questionnaire. Trial terms last two weeks and “trial date” means jury selection.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — Courtroom and trial protocol (trap)
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. Courtroom and trial protocol (trap): Stand when addressing the court or questioning witnesses, speak from the lectern or counsel table, and ask leave before approaching a witness each time. Address others formally. Bring the original and three copies of all exhibits in separate D-ring binders, pre-marked, with three copies of witness and exhibit lists for the courtroom deputy; for voluminous exhibits, contact the court the week before trial about electronic copies. State the legal basis for every objection; only the attorney examining a witness may object during another party’s examination of that witness. In openings and closings, stay at least 15 feet from the jury box. After-hours informal communications go to chambers email with opposing counsel copied, but they do not preserve the record.

docs.t: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr. (M.D. Ala.) — AI use
docs.x: Judge R. Austin Huffaker Jr., M.D. Ala.. AI use: AI tools are permitted but require close supervision and citation-checking; anyone who discovers fabricated citations must raise it immediately, and presenting false or hallucinated citations draws sanctions or striking of the filing.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Motion hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Motion hearings (trap): The court does not generally schedule motion hearings; scheduling is the parties’ job. To get a hearing, contact the courtroom deputy, Kelly Anglim (Kelly_Anglim@vawd.uscourts.gov or 540-857-5117). If the parties do not promptly schedule one, the court rules without a hearing. Nondispositive motions, including motions for more time, opposed or not, may be decided at any time without awaiting a response. Dispositive motions and motions to exclude experts must be heard no later than 45 days before trial; motions in limine (including objections to deposition testimony and trial exhibits) no later than the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Briefing and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Briefing and page limits (trap): A supporting brief must accompany every pretrial motion unless the motion itself contains the legal argument or is certified unopposed. Oppositions are due 14 days after service of the movant’s brief (7 days for motions in limine and other trial-related motions); a late opposition means the motion is treated as unopposed, absent good cause. Replies are due 7 days after the opposition (for trial-related motions, 7 days or at least 2 days before the final pretrial conference, whichever is shorter). No surreply without prior leave. Briefs are capped at 25 pages, exclusive of exhibits, with standard margins and double spacing, unless leave is first obtained for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Courtesy copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Proposed orders go to Dillon.ecf@vawd.uscourts.gov as a Word attachment, copied to all opposing counsel or unrepresented parties; proposed orders filed in CM/ECF should also be emailed separately in Word.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Sealing: No motion, brief, or exhibit may be filed under seal except as allowed by General Local Rule 9, and a stipulated protective order or other agreement cannot modify its requirements.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Scheduling and discovery (sample order)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Scheduling and discovery (sample order): Typical deadlines: Rule 26(f) conference 14 days from the order; initial disclosures 30 days (plaintiff) and 45 days (defendant); joinder and amendment 120 days; discovery closes 95 days before trial, with written discovery served in time for responses by the cutoff; dispositive motions and motions to exclude experts filed 80 days before trial. The parties may amend the disclosure and discovery provisions by agreement without leave but must then file a Rule 26(f) plan; changing any other deadline requires a motion and a proposed agreed order. Do not file discovery materials unless relevant to a motion or required.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Experts
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Experts: Retained-expert reports are due 90 days (plaintiff) and 60 days (defendant) before the discovery deadline. Non-retained experts (such as treating physicians) must be disclosed with Rule 26(a)(2)(C) information within 80 days (plaintiff) and 110 days (defendant) of the order; rebuttal under Rule 26(a)(2)(D). A motion to exclude an expert is due by the summary judgment deadline and is not a “motion in limine,” however titled.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Pretrial and trial: Trial starts at 9:00 a.m. Contact the courtroom deputy to set a final pretrial conference no later than 7 days before trial. Exchange and file witness lists (name, address, and testimony summary) and exhibit lists 28 days before trial; motions in limine are due 21 days before trial. Deposition designations 21 days before trial; counterdesignations and objections 14 days; objections to counterdesignations 7 days before trial or at least 2 days before the final pretrial conference, whichever is shorter. Parties must confer in good faith, at length if necessary, to resolve objections before the conference. Jury trials: file proposed jury instructions and special interrogatories 7 days before trial and email them in Word, with citations, to dillon.ecf@vawd.uscourts.gov; email a joint statement of the case (or separate ones if no agreem

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Settlement and dismissal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. Settlement and dismissal (trap): If the case settles and the court does not receive a proposed final order within 30 days after notice of settlement, the case will be dismissed with prejudice. A party wanting the court to retain jurisdiction to enforce the settlement must move within 60 days of the dismissal order. Mediation by a magistrate judge is available on any party’s motion.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — ERISA benefits cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. ERISA benefits cases (trap): The proposed ERISA order becomes the scheduling order unless a party objects within 10 days. Any discovery is due within 60 days, and the administrator or fiduciary must file the administrative record within 60 days. All parties are deemed to have moved for summary judgment on the record. Plaintiff’s brief (with any authenticity objections to the record) is due 30 days after service of the record, defendant’s response 30 days later, and an optional reply 7 days later. Oral argument must be requested promptly after the last brief by contacting Judicial Assistant Miriam Frazier (miriamf@vawd.uscourts.gov or 540-857-5120); otherwise the court rules on the papers. Deadlines may be moved by filed written stipulation, but no more than 60 days without leave.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Appearances and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Appearances and contact (trap): All hearings are attended by counsel in person unless prior leave is timely sought and granted. No ex parte communication with the judge or staff about a pending case without prior leave; violations without good cause draw sanctions. Counsel may contact the courtroom manager (Tammy Kimura, 808-541-3073) about continuances and similar scheduling relief. Nothing may be faxed to chambers without prior permission from chambers staff.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Summary judgment (trap): Only one Rule 56 motion per party without leave, sought by noticed motion showing good cause. An early motion (for example, on immunity) followed by a later motion after more discovery is an example of good cause.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Motions in limine (trap): Due 3 weeks before trial; responses due 2 weeks before trial; no replies. Motions and oppositions are limited to 5 pages, and they are generally heard at the final pretrial conference. Meet and confer under Local Rule 7.8 at least 7 days before filing. No Daubert motions once trial has begun.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Electronic devices
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Electronic devices: In the courtroom, only attorneys of record may use devices, only for the ongoing case-related proceeding and with court approval. Phones off on entering the courtroom; no cameras or recording in the courtroom or chambers. The order does not authorize bringing devices to the courthouse for other matters. Violations draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Trial schedule and jury selection
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Trial schedule and jury selection: Jury trials run 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. with no lunch break (bring a snack); some days may run later. Jury selection days run 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with lunch about noon to 1:30 p.m. Non-jury trials run 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., sometimes longer. The court conducts general voir dire, incorporating parties’ special questions; each side then gets a maximum of 20 minutes. Peremptories use the open, alternate-strike method on a court form. Jurors may take notes.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Exhibits and witnesses (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Exhibits and witnesses (trap): Meet and confer on a common exhibit set and try to stipulate to authenticity and admissibility; no statement of objections need be filed despite the Rule 16 order. File exhibit lists by the final pretrial conference date. Exhibits go in 3-ring binders no larger than 3 inches at the spine; one original and two copies are due the Thursday before trial. Disclose the next day’s witnesses to counsel and the court by 4:30 p.m. the prior business day; undisclosed witnesses may not testify.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Demonstratives and deposition testimony
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Demonstratives and deposition testimony: No demonstratives in opening, and no material not in evidence during examination or closing, without all parties’ consent or (failing agreement) leave of court, obtained in advance without delaying the jury. Exhibits are generally not passed among jurors. Use the microphone (lapel mics on request). For published deposition testimony, give timely notice; counsel generally meet with the court by the prior trial day to resolve objections, and the offering party provides a revised designation transcript by the start of that trial day, plus a reader if read aloud.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Jury instructions and pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Jury instructions and pretrial filings: Comply with Local Rule 51.1; L.R. 51.1(b) and (e)–(j) also apply to verdict forms. Submit instructions and verdict forms in hard copy and in Word by disk or email to watson_orders@hid.uscourts.gov. Each juror gets a copy. File a joint, brief, objective statement of the case for voir dire 2 weeks before trial. Counsel arrange their own interpreters well ahead, get advance permission for special equipment, and give the courtroom manager after-hours phone numbers before trial.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Summary judgment concise statements (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Summary judgment concise statements (trap): The separate concise statement is limited to 5 pages or 1500 words, includes only material facts absolutely necessary to the motion, and contains no argument. Facts in the moving party’s statement are deemed admitted unless controverted in the opposing concise statement. Support each fact with specific evidence, identifying the filing, the portion and page, and where it is found in ECF; highlight or otherwise emphasize the relevant portions. Documents need not be filed in full. File the concise statement separately, not as an attachment to the motion. All exhibits on originals and courtesy copies need labeled tabs. The memo attaches example moving and opposing statements (two-column facts and evidence format).

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Continuing trial
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Continuing trial: All motions to continue trial filed within 30 days of the trial date are heard by Judge Gillmor.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Rule 404(b) notice in criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Rule 404(b) notice in criminal cases (trap): Oral statements do not satisfy 404(b) notice in felony trials before Judge Gillmor. At the final pretrial conference before the magistrate judge, the government will be required to file and serve, within two days, written notice describing the 404(b) evidence with enough particularity for the defendant to identify the act. The defendant files and serves a written response within two days after the notice is filed.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Trial days and out-of-jury matters
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Trial days and out-of-jury matters: Jury trial sessions are Tuesday to Friday; in a week with a Monday holiday, Wednesday to Friday. At recesses and at the end of each session, once the jury leaves, the court asks whether counsel have matters for the record. Offers of proof, preservation of objections, motions to reconsider evidentiary rulings, and witness or scheduling discussions happen then.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Objections at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Objections at trial (trap): Counsel must rise and wait to be recognized before stating an objection, and state it in five words or less (for example, “Objection - Hearsay”). The court will rule, ask for a short response or explanation, or call a sidebar. docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Multi-volume and sealed appendices: Split into consecutively numbered volumes if the appendix exceeds the e-filing size limit or contains sealed material. Pagination runs continuously across volumes, no document is split between volumes, every volume’s table of contents covers the whole appendix, and each cover page states its App.__ range. When moving to seal, file a public volume and a separate sealed volume numbered “Sealed.App.1” onward and cited as “Sealed.App.__.” A sealed item’s description in the public table of contents may be generic or omitted if needed.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Joint discovery and case management plan
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Joint discovery and case management plan: The judge’s Joint Discovery and Case Management Plan form asks for jurisdiction details (for LLCs, LLPs, and partnerships, every member’s citizenship, plus an attached affidavit or declaration), removal service dates, the elements of each claim and defense with supporting authority, related cases, unserved parties, and discovery, settlement, ADR, and consent positions. Attach a proposed scheduling order on the court’s Word form, replacing its bracketed presumptive intervals with calendar dates, and explain any material deviation. The ADR and settlement items satisfy the Local Rule CV-88 report. Counsel must state they have read and will comply with the standing orders on the court’s website.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Scheduling and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Scheduling and extensions (trap): Presumptive civil schedule: motions to add parties or amend 30 days after the initial pretrial conference; burden-of-proof experts 180 days later; opposing experts 30 days after that; discovery closes 60 days later (requests must be answerable by then); mediation or settlement conference 21 days later; all motions except in limine 21 days after that. Parties may agree to extend discovery deadlines with written notice if later deadlines are unaffected, but the court can reject the extension. Non-discovery deadlines and continuances will not be extended, even on joint motion, without actual diligence and extraordinary cause. Rebuttal experts are due 30 days after the disclosure being rebutted. Attorney’s-fees experts are exempt; fees are sought by Rule 54(d)(2) motion after judgment.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Motions: No motion other than in limine after the motion deadline without good cause. If no dispositive motion is filed, the parties must jointly file a notice saying so, so trial can be set.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Mediation and settlement (trap)

A joint report signed by all counsel (date, attendees and capacities, whether meaningful progress was made, and prospects) is due within 7 days.

Under the scheduling orders, a referred magistrate judge may adjust scheduling order dates.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Sanctions and pet peeves
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Sanctions and pet peeves: The most common grounds for sanctions are discovery abuse and failing to appear for scheduled hearings. The court will not tolerate tardiness or unpreparedness.

The order notes, among other things, that private process server fees, postage, faxes, electronic legal research, travel, meals, and mediation fees generally are not recoverable, document translation is not interpreter compensation, and video and transcript versions of a deposition each require a showing of necessity.

docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. If the other side disagrees with how the facts are characterized, it must tell the court within 3 days. The order is docketed in all pending and future “463 Habeas Corpus – Alien Detainee” cases assigned to the judge.

docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Social Security referrals: Social Security appeals assigned to the judge are referred to an El Paso magistrate judge for nondispositive pretrial matters and findings and recommendations on dispositive motions.

docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Chambers contacts: The judge is a Senior U.S. District Judge in El Paso (525 Magoffin Avenue). The page lists the courtroom deputy and court reporter but no further hearing or filing procedures.

docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Final pretrial conference: At least one attorney who will try the case for each party, and any unrepresented party, must attend. docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Hearings and contact
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Procedural questions not answered by the rules or standing orders may go to the law clerks at (915) 534-6740. Notify a law clerk immediately when a pending motion is resolved, and notify the court immediately when a motion is unopposed or the case settles. No chambers copies are required. For a TRO, after filing and assignment notify a law clerk or the courtroom deputy, try to give the other side notice, and send it a copy by fax or email.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Civil motion format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Civil motion format (trap): Every civil motion, opposition, and reply must contain: only the title below the caption on page 1; a statement of issues of no more than 1 page; a succinct statement of facts; argument with authority; and, if over 10 pages, a table of contents and table of authorities. The title page, tables, and statement of issues do not count toward the CV-7 page limit. Noncompliant filings will not be accepted. Longer briefs need leave (routinely granted); additional briefing beyond the reply needs leave; no letter briefs. Do not combine a motion to dismiss with an answer, or a response with a motion, in one document. Hyperlinking citations to Westlaw or Lexis is encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Pretrial deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Pretrial deadlines (trap): File the joint Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting (Appendix A form) within 45 days after any defendant appears (including by answer, removal, motion to dismiss, or transfer); missing it draws a show-cause order. A motion to dismiss does not stay discovery. Changes need a particularized showing of good cause, and extending one deadline does not extend later ones. Requests to modify the scheduling order must be by motion; any request to move the trial date must be made in writing before the discovery deadline.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Summary judgment

The opposition’s “Response to Proposed Undisputed Facts” admits or denies each paragraph and lists “Disputed Issues of Material Fact” in a separate section. Each fact and denial needs a specific citation to competent affidavits or admissible evidence, filed with the statements; failing to cite can lead to denial or grant of the motion. Movants against a pro se party must serve the order’s form notice with Rule 56 and the order attached.
